recipes.instructions:
Fill a 14-16-quart pot with two quarts of water and bring to a boil.
Meanwhile, peel and devein the shrimp, keeping the heads and hulls. Set the shrimp aside in cold water. In the large "gumbo pot" boil heads and hulls for 30 minutes to an hour. This will give you Creole gumbo. Strain shrimp heads and hulls from stock and set aside. Discard heads and hull immediately. Otherwise, the next day your kitchen will smell like Bayou St. John.
Clean the fresh crabs  If the crabs are fresh, you must take time to clean them. Discard the hard back shell and some of the so-called "dead man," or yellow insides. Clean and separate crabs and set aside. (Note: If necessary, you can use meat from king, Dungeness, snow or stone crabs for your gumbo).
Before you fire up the stove again, cut up your celery, parsley, peppers, onions and garlic, especially if you're alone and there is no one to help you stir the pots. It takes time peeling the onions and garlic  Put the celery and parsley in a separate container from the other chopped ingredients and refrigerate until needed to keep them fresh.
Place the gumbo pot with the shrimp stock on the stove. Add cleaned crabs and bay leaves. Stir slowly. You don't want your shrimp stock messing up the floor. Add celery, parsley, and tomato paste to the gumbo brewing on the stove. Bring to a boil. Turn down heat, cover, and let simmer.
Here comes the roux -- a thick and flavorful sauce that has become one of the most important staples of Louisiana cuisine. Pour oil or shortening into a separate heavy skillet (please do not use a thin omelet pan) over a medium-low heat. Slowly stir in flour to make the roux. Keep your eyes on the skillet. If the phone rings, let the answering machine pick it up. Cook roux until it has a dark mahogany color. Do not stop stirring until roux appears nutty or grainy. If black specks appear, the roux is burned. Throw it out and start from scratch. A good roux could take 30 to 45 minutes cooking time.
Now you are ready to add the holy trinity of onions, garlic, and green peppers to the roux mixture. Stir ingredients in slowly because the flour is still sizzling. The moisture will begin to disappear. This is when Jean would add another quart or two of water to the gumbo pot. Add roux to the gumbo pot. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Lower heat and cover. The kitchen should smell good right now. Pour yourself another cold something-or-other. You're halfway there. Come back to look and stir in an hour or so.
Season to taste: add salt, pepper, thyme, Worcestershire sauce, Tabasco sauce and any Creole seasoning you like. Don't overdo it right now. Let the roux work its magic absorbing all the wonderful ingredients. Gumbo is usually very spicy, but you can keep it mild. Remember, if you have decided to use andouille sausage it is also hot.
Fry sausages and okra with a little bit of the leftover grease. Sprinkle a little leftover flour if the okra is fresh. Add to gumbo pot. Add chopped peeled tomatoes, stirring until well blended. Add more water if necessary. The roux will keep it thick and tasty. Return to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes. Reduce heat and let simmer, uncovered, for 2 1/2 to 3 hours over low heat.
Skim any excess fat. Add shrimp. Stir in slowly as you increase the heat one last time. It's time to stir in the fil powder. Cook another 20 to 30 minutes until the gumbo is thick. Taste and adjust seasonings one more time. Did I mention the rice? Seafood gumbo is served over Louisiana rice. Of course, you can substitute for your own favorite rice. Just plain old brown or white rice will do. Before serving, taste one more time and adjust seasoning. Turn off heat and remove seafood gumbo from the stove.
To cool down the pot before serving, place it in the sink with a few inches of ice-cold water. If needed, add additional salt and Tabasco sauce. If you can see through the gumbo to the bottom of the pot, work on your roux next time.

recipes.instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400 degrees f. Season the shrimp with salt & pepper, refrigerate until ready to use. Grease a 13x9-inch baking dish.
  2. Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat until the oil is shimmering. Add the onion, fennel bulb and 1/2 t. salt. Cook, stirring frequently until the vegetables are softened and starting to brown around the edges, about 10 minutes. Add the minced garlic and crushed red pepper flakes, cook and stir until the garlic becomes very fragrant, about 30 seconds.
  3. Add the orzo to the vegetables, stir to coat the orzo with oil, continue cooking, stirring fairly constantly, about 4 minutes, until the orzo has a toasty aroma. Add the wine, cook,stirring constantly, until the liquid evaporates, about 1 minute. Add the chicken broth, water and 1/4 t. salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, simmer, until the orzo is almost completely tender, about 12 minutes, stirring fairly constantly to prevent sticking and adjusting the heat as necessary to maintain a lively simmer.
  4. After the 12 minutes, remove from heat and stir in the shrimp, tomatoes, oregano and 1 T. of the parsley. Transfer to the prepared baking dish, sprinkle with the feta. Bake for about 20 minutes, until the shrimp is cooked through and the feta is lightly browned. Before serving, sprinkle with the remaining parsley and the reserved fennel fronds. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.instructions:
1.Firstly, to cook the shrimp, heat the olive oil in a pan and once hot add the shrimp crushed garlic and chili flakes. It is important to get the oil nice and hot (not smoking, just before that point) your shrimp should sizzle when added to the pan. Check the back of the shrimp and when you see the colour change about half way up, turn them over. Do the same on the other side. This should only take a minute to two minutes maximum on both sides  otherwise you will get a rubbery result if you leave it too long. Squeeze over the lime juice  this too should bubble and reduce. Add a little salt and pepper, stir through, remove from the heat and set aside.
2.Mix the dressing ingredients together, check for flavour, adjust if need be and set aside.
3.Place all the salad ingredients in a bowl except the avocado and the salt and pepper. Prepare the avocado as you are about to serve otherwise it will turn brown. Once it is covered in the lime dressing, this will slow down the oxidization process and it wont go brown so easily.
4.When you are ready to serve mix  of the avocado through the salad and add the dressing. Toss everything together. Taste to see if you need any salt and pepper. Place your shrimp on top of the salad with the rest of the avocado and sprinkle/pour any residue from the pan over your salad in which you cooked the shrimp. This is great flavour, so you dont want to lose it.

recipes.instructions:
To prepare the pork filling -
Mince 700g of pork and place them in a large mixing bowl. Add 2 tablespoons of corn starch, 1 teaspoon of salt, 1 teaspoon of ground white pepper,  1/2 teaspoon of sugar, 1 teaspoon of Maggie Seasoning Sauce or Worcestershire sauce, 2 tablespoons of Shaoxing Huatiao wine and 2 tablespoons of sesame oil.
Roughly chop 80g of water chestnuts into fine pieces. I used canned ones.
Chop 4 large Chinese mushrooms into fine pieces too.
Add the water chestnuts and mushrooms to the pork mixture. Mix all the ingredients well to combine.
Finely dice a small carrot. These will be placed on top each pork siew mai to garnish. Use salmon roe or salted egg yolk if preferred.
Set aside the pork mixture and the diced carrots till ready to wrap dumplings.

To make the glutinous rice filling -
Soak 2 lap cheongs (Chinese sausages) in boiling water until the skin is separated from the meat. Remove the skin from the lap cheong and cut them into small dices.
In a large sauce pan over medium-high heat, pan fry the lap cheong dices until they are golden but not brown. They should be a lovely red.
Follow the instructions at Glutinous Rice in Lotus Leaf (http://cooking.storyofbing.com/2010/07/glutinous-rice-in-lotus-leaf-2/) and prepare the glutinous rice. Once the rice and other ingredients are stir fried till fragrant, add the pieces of fried lap cheong and set aside to cool.

Prepare the ingredients necessary for the wrapping of the dumplings.
Start by placing a sheet of wonton wrapper on a flat surface. Place a small teaspoon of filling in the centre of the wonton wrapper.
Dap finger in some water and gently wet the sides of the wonton wrapper.
Gather the wonton wrapper with the filling in the palm of hand and squeeze gently while folding the wrapper skin upwards and against the filling so that the wonton wrapper wraps the filling tightly.
Make sure the dumplings are tight. Otherwise they may fall apart while being steamed. Use more water to seal them if necessary.
Place a large shrimp on the top of each pork siew mai.
Add a few pieces of chopped carrot or salmon roe or salted egg yolk to add a fresh colour to the dumpling.
Do the same for the glutinous rice siew mai, adding more lap cheong pieces on the top if preferred.
Place the dumplings in a steamer lined with baking paper. Cut some holes through the baking paper to let the steam through.
Place the steamer over boiling water for 14-15 minutes or until the filling is cooked.
Serve hot.
Uncooked dumplings may be frozen and steamed at a later date. Dust some flour in a container so that the dumplings wont stick to it.

Preheat your oven to 375F and set the top rack to the middle position (BTW, this recipe is a great toaster oven candidate).  Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil or a nonstick cooking mat.
In a large bowl, combine the crab meat, diced red bell pepper, half of the diced green onion (reserving the other half) and half of the bread crumbs (reserving the other half).  Mix in the honey and chili powder, then season to taste with salt and pepper.
I like to form my crab cakes by pressing them into a 1/2 cup measure, squeezing tightly so theyll hold their shape. Meanwhile, fry the bacon or prosciutto in a large skillet until crispy.  Set aside to drain, then crumble into small pieces using a sharp knife.
Finely chop the spinach and watercress stems.  In a large skillet, melt the butter over medium heat.  Add the garlic and saut 1 minute.  Then, add the remaining green onion, bread crumbs and watercress stems.  Saut 1 minute more.  Finally, add the chopped spinach and cook until wilted, 1-2 minutes.  Season to taste with salt and pepper.
To serve, plate a crab cake atop a smear of the spinach mixture, then sprinkle the whole plate with crumbled bacon.

1. Begin by mixing all of your marinade ingredients together and pouring it over the salmon in a big baggy or container. Marinate under refrigeration for at least a half an hour or up to 2 hours.

  8. After ~10-13 minutes, salmon will be finished. Flip the smooth side of the banana leaves up and make a slit through them to serve....they kinda look like tamales, huh!
  9. I served with chinese noodles, corn and the dipping sauce.

recipes.instructions: Rinse the black-eyed peas and soak in several inches of water for 6 hours or overnight. Drain and rinse, then transfer to a large saucepan and cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 40 to 60 minutes. Take care not to overcook  the beans should be tender but not be falling apart. Drain and set aside.To prepare the eggplant, cut of the stem and bottom edge and then cut in half lengthwise. Score the flesh into diagonal 1-inch lines, then turn and score again until you have a diagonal pattern. Take care not to cut through the skin. Sprinkle with some salt and let sit for 40 minutes. Rinse and squeeze out any excess water. Brush the eggplant with some oil and transfer to a roasting pan. Bake in a preheated 400 oven until the flesh appears collapsed and is wrinkly. Remove from heat and let cool for about 10 minutes, season with a bit of salt, and remove the flesh from the eggplant. If there is too much water, drain in a strainer. Set aside.Heat the oil over medium heat in the same saucepan used to cook the black-eyed peas. When hot, toss in the shallots and chilies and saut for 2 to 3 minutes. Now add the spices and stir for another minute, until fragrant. Add the tomato, cook for another few minutes, and then add the eggplant and black-eyed peas, and cook for another few minutes, stirring often.Pour a few tablespoons of water into the pan and add handfuls of chard at a time until wilted. Add more water as necessary. Add the lemon juice and salt to taste near the end of the cooking time. Remove from heat, cover, and let sit for a few minutes before serving.

Drain and rinse, then transfer to a large saucepan and cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 40 to 60 minutes. Take care not to overcook  the beans should be tender but not be falling apart.

Drain and set aside.To prepare the eggplant, cut of the stem and bottom edge and then cut in half lengthwise. Score the flesh into diagonal 1-inch lines, then turn and score again until you have a diagonal pattern. Take care not to cut through the skin.
Sprinkle with some salt and let sit for 40 minutes. Rinse and squeeze out any excess water.
Brush the eggplant with some oil and transfer to a roasting pan.
Bake in a preheated 400 oven until the flesh appears collapsed and is wrinkly.
Remove from heat and let cool for about 10 minutes, season with a bit of salt, and remove the flesh from the eggplant. If there is too much water, drain in a strainer. Set aside.

Heat the oil over medium heat in the same saucepan used to cook the black-eyed peas. When hot, toss in the shallots and chilies and saut for 2 to 3 minutes. Now add the spices and stir for another minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomato, cook for another few minutes, and then add the eggplant and black-eyed peas, and cook for another few minutes, stirring often.
Pour a few tablespoons of water into the pan and add handfuls of chard at a time until wilted.
Add more water as necessary.
Add the lemon juice and salt to taste near the end of the cooking time.
Remove from heat, cover, and let sit for a few minutes before serving.

recipes.instructions:
1. Set the nuts to soak in a bowl of water 2-8 hours before preparing the meat.
  2. Preheat the oven to 375 F and line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
  3. Finely chop the cauliflower into rice-sized pieces, or pulse in the food processor until the desired consistency. Toss with the oil and spread onto the baking sheet in an even layer. Bake for 18 minutes, stirring halfway through.
  4. While the cauliflower rice is cooking, prepare the guacamole and taco meat.
  5. Cut the avocado into large chunks and place into a small bowl. Add the lime juice and mash the avocado to a chunky puree or your preferred consistency. Stir in the cilantro, jalapeno, onion and spices. Set aside.
  6. Remove the nuts from the water and place into a small food processor. Discard the water. Pulse the nuts until theyve reached a ground meat consistency, I find about 5-7 pulses works. Transfer to a bowl and stir in the salt, cumin, garlic powder, and red chili powder. Set aside.
  7. When the cauliflower is done, transfer to a mixing bowl while still warm and stir in the lime, cilantro, and salt.
  8. To assemble the bowls, layer 1 cup of the cauliflower rice in a bowl with taco nut meat, a dollop of guacamole, fresh tomatoes, and a sprinkling of fresh cilantro.
  9. Serve immediately with an additional slice of lime if desired.

recipes.instructions:
1. Place chopped thyme, lemon juice and zest and garlic in a glass bowl. Microwave on high heat for 30 seconds then let the herbs seep in the warm olive oil while you prepare the artichokes.
  2. Prepare a large pot with an inch of water at the bottom and a steamer rack. Prepare the artichokes. Have lemon wedges ready. If you want a nice presentation, use scissors to snip away the pointy tips of the artichoke leaves. As you trim the artichokes, rub the cut areas with juice from the lemon wedges to prevent the artichokes from turning brown. Use a vegetable peeler to cut away the thick outer layer of the artichoke stems. Trim the stems to 2 inches from the base of the artichoke. Cut off and discard the top 1/2 inch of the artichokes. Cut the artichokes in half. Use a strong metal spoon to scoop out the fuzzy chokes and the small inner artichoke leaves. Rub lemon juice all over the inside and exposed cut areas of the artichokes.
  3. Heat the water in the large pot with a steamer rack on high. When it comes to a boil, reduce the heat to medium high and place the artichoke halves, cut side down on the steam rack. Cover. Steam for 20 minutes or until you can easily pull off the outer leaves, and you can pierce the heart easily with a knife. The artichokes can be just a tiny bit less cooked than would be typically perfect for steamed artichokes, as you will be cooking them further on the grill.
  4. Prepare your grill for direct, high heat. Toss the artichokes in the garlic, lemon and thyme infused oil coating liberally. Sprinkle artichokes with salt and pepper. Place the artichoke halves cut-side-down on the grill grates. Cover, and grill for 5 to 10 minutes, until you have nice grill mark on the cut sides of the artichokes.

recipes.instructions:
1. To make sweet tart dough:
  2. Mix flour and salt.
  3. Melt coconut oil, then stir with flour and salt until mixture resembles coarse meal.
  4. Add maple syrup gradually (if dough does not hold together on its own, add just enough ice water to hold dough together).
  5. Mix until a soft workable ball forms in the bowl; do not overmix.
  6. Add a small amount of flour if necessary.
  7. Shape the dough with your hands into a flattened disc.
  8. Roll dough out between two sheets of parchment paper; dust flour over the bottom sheet and on top of the dough.
  9. Use quick gentle strokes to start rolling from the center outward in each direction, like a compass.
  10. Transfer the parchment covered dough onto a baking sheet.
  11. Refrigerate the dough on the baking sheet while preparing the blueberry filling.
  12. To make blueberry basil filling:
  13. Preheat oven to 350 F.
  14. In a medium bowl, whisk 1/4 cup of the sugar, arrowroot powder, and sea salt together.
  15. Rinse and drain blueberries in a strainer, then transfer to a towel and blot dry.
  16. Gently stir in blueberries, basil, lemon zest, and lemon juice; set aside.
  17. Remove dough from refrigerator.
  18. Peel off top layer of parchment paper.
  19. Pour blueberry filling over tart dough, leaving a 2-inch border.
  20. Fold the dough border over the blueberry filling to form a pleated ruffle.
  21. Brush the folded dough border with 2 teaspoons oil, then pat the berries with the rest.
  22. Sprinkle the crust with 2 teaspoons of sugar.
  23. Bake about 45-55 minutes, or until the galette is golden and thick juices bubble on top.
  24. Cool completely before serving.

recipes.instructions:
Soak the dates in hot water while you get the rest of the ingredients and start on step 2 (about 5 minutes). The water should be hot to the touch but not hot enough to burn you.
Process the almonds in a food processor until coarse almond meal is formed. Add the pecans and process until they are ground up into a coarse meal as well.
Drain the dates and use your hand to squeeze out excess water. Add the drained dates, cocoa powder, vanilla extract, agave nectar, and salt to the food processor. Process until a smooth paste forms.
Use a tablespoon measure to help you form the truffles. Pack a heaping tablespoon of the mixture into the tablespoon measure  really pack it in there. Use your fingers to slide the half-rounded ball out of the tablespoon measure, and then use your hands to form a tightly packed ball of truffle goodness. Be gentle with them  I found that they fall apart if you try to roll them into balls. It is best to squish them with your hand into perfect little spheres.
Form truffles until you use up all the mixture. The last bit that was not enough for a truffle went straight into my mouth. :)
If you choose to, gently roll the truffles in the toppings of your choice. I had some turtle crunch sprinkles, unsweetened coconut flakes, and extra cocoa powder. The cocoa powder definitely gives the the truffles an extra dark chocolate kick, so if you dont like the bitterness of the cocoa powder then dont use that as a topping.

  3. Whisk the pear juice with the lemon juice and a small pinch of salt. Add some simple syrup or water to thin slightly, if necessary. Try Linguican and Rice Stuffed Bell Peppers, Stuffed Bell Peppers with Chicken Italian Sausage, Rice, and Spinach, and Blast of Color Mexican Stuffed Bell Peppers with Chicken and Rice for similar recipes.
recipes.instructions:
1. Cut tops off peppers, remove seeds and wash.
  2. Saute onions with olive oil lightly.
  3. Stir in chopped tomatoes and tomato paste.
  4. Saut for 3 more minutes.
  5. Add the rice and braise for 5 minutes.
  6. Then add salt, sugar, the spices and, hot water.
  7. Simmer until all liquid is evaporated.
  8. Let it cool for a while.
  9. With a spoon fill the peppers with the mixture.
  10. Place one slice of tomato as a cap on top of each pepper.
  11. In a large saucepan or pot, place the rice stuffed bell peppers. Add water, enough to almost cover half height of the peppers.
  12. Close the lid and cook on low heat, for about 15-20 minutes.
  13. Serve warm or hot.
  14. ENJOY

trailData.name: Amicalola Falls via East Ridge Loop Trail
trailData.description: This route combines the Appalachian Trail and the East Ridge Trail to form a spectacular loop that visits the tallest waterfall in Georgia. The trail winds through dense woodlands along a well-maintained path with various viewpoints scattered throughout. A series of staircases lead up to the falls viewpoint, which is the most challenging part of the hike. Amicalola Falls stands an impressive 729 feet and cascades down rock ledges.  The trail then connects with the East Ridge Trail, which...

trailData.name: Cloudland Canyon West Rim Loop
trailData.description: This trail showcases the breathtaking scenery of Cloudland Canyon, the forests, and cascading waterfalls. The route progresses into the canyon on a 40-degree slope, which can be steep. Most of the trail consists of gravel with a mix of staircases along the way. There are two magnificent waterfalls that cascade off sheer rock faces. Keep in mind that swimming and climbing on rocks are strictly forbidden, and regulations are enforced.

trailData.name: Cherokee Falls and Hemlock Falls Trail
trailData.description:
This trail is a lot of fun and offers plenty of scenic views. However, it should be noted that there are a lot of stairs, some of which are metal grates, making it less dog-friendly. Additionally, the waterfalls may dry up depending on the time of year. The trail can be quite rocky and rooted, so it's important to be aware of your footing. Keep in mind that the hike out is all uphill, so be sure to save some energy for the journey back.

While dogs are allowed in this area, bringing them on...

trailData.name: Indian Seats Trail
trailData.description:
The Indian Seats Trail leads to a beautiful overlook in Sawnee Mountain Preserve. It’s a well-marked and well-maintained trail with some short steep sections, roots, and rocks along the way, but nothing too difficult to manage.

You will be rewarded with stunning views of the North Georgia mountains. Make sure to stick to the track—it's easy to take the wrong path back.

trailData.area_name: Vickery Creek Unit- Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area
trailData.name: Vickery Creek Trail
trailData.location_label: Vickery Creek Unit- Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: This is a favorite route in the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area and offers an escape into the woodlands of north Georgia. For some portions, the trail winds through lush greenery with Big Creek along the side. As hikers venture along the trail, they'll come across the historic Roswell Mill Ruins, which is a 19th-century textile mills factory.

trailData.name: Stone Mountain Walk-Up Trail
trailData.description:
One of the most popular hikes in the Atlanta area is at Stone Mountain. This hike is suitable for all ages and there is plenty of parking available at the base.

The hike itself takes place entirely on smooth granite rock. Although there is a defined route, the trail can be quite wide and there are many trees on the rock face.

For those who prefer not to hike, there is also a gondola available to take visitors to the top of the mountain for a small fee.

trailData.name: Stone Mountain Cherokee Loop
trailData.description:
This is a great family-friendly trail with a nice variety of terrain and scenery. The trail is well-maintained, and there are beautiful overlooks to get different vantage points of Stone Mountain. 

The last mile of the trail on the Cherokee loop has a steep, rocky section that can get slippery when wet. Please use caution and wear appropriate footwear.

trailData.name: Homestead Trail
trailData.location_label: Red Top Mountain State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: The trail starts at the Visitor Center and goes through gently rolling hills, winding through a beautiful forest. After the first mile, there is a road crossing at Lodge Road. Once you cross the road, the trail forms a loop that follows the scenic shores of Lake Allatoona. Along the way, you will pass through forests, fields, and get to see the chimney of an old homestead home. This hike offers the most diverse and beautiful scenery of all the trails in Red Top.

trailData.name: Pigeon Hill to East and West Loop Trail
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: Pigeon Hill and Burnt Hickory loops is located near Marietta, Georgia. The trail is great for hiking and normally takes 1-3 hours

trailData.name: East Palisades Trail and Bamboo Forest
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: This hiking trail offers spectacular views of Georgia's Chattahoochee River and is just a short drive from Atlanta. Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area (CRNRA) preserves a 48-mile stretch of the Chattahoochee River in North Georgia between Atlanta and Lake Lanier. Based within the Indian Trail District of the CRNRA, the East Palisades Trail features a loop trail of high, rocky bluffs offering breathtaking views of the river. It's popular for trail running, hiking, fishing, and...

trailData.area_name: Island Ford Unit - Chattahoochee   River National Recreation Area
trailData.name: Island Ford Trail
trailData.location_label: Island Ford Unit - Chattahoochee   River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: Island Ford Park is located alongside the picturesque Chattahoochee River and offers a peaceful and family-friendly environment with its many trails. This route takes you through several trails in the park, providing you with a relaxing walk along the riverbank and through the woods. For those interested in history, there are numerous historical markers with interpretive signs that provide an opportunity to learn about the area's past.

trailData.name: Gold Branch Trail
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: The walking trail system runs along the Chattahoochee River and offers a diverse range of terrain, including woods, rivers, hills, flat surfaces, rocky paths, and pine straw-covered paths. While there are some slight inclines, they are not too steep. The trail passes over a few small creeks, runs alongside Bull Sluice Lake, and ends at the old car in the forest. The majority of the path is covered by trees.

trailData.name: Iron Hill Loop
trailData.location_label: Red Top Mountain State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This is a gravel trail that is perfect for a short hike. The trail is well-marked and offers beautiful scenery. Along the way, there are numerous benches and opportunities to walk off the path and get closer to the lake. This multi-use trail is ideal for hiking, trail running, and biking. The path is mostly flat with a few small hills to make it more interesting.

trailData.area_name: Jones Bridge Unit - Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area
trailData.name: Jones Bridge Trail
trailData.location_label: Jones Bridge Unit - Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: The trail is mostly flat and follows the river, but there are a few climbs when the trail moves away from the river's edge. Maps at trail intersections make navigation very easy. There are several footbridges, some aluminum, and some wooden. At the south end of the trail lies the Chattahoochee River Environmental Education Center. The trail is nicely shaded and offers excellent views of the river, as well as ample opportunities to spot wildlife.

trailData.name: Sweetwater Creek Red Trail
trailData.description: The route offers a pleasant trail with an exceptional overlook, but be cautious as it becomes quite rocky with the river nearby. The climb over the rocks and roots can be challenging and technical. However, the breathtaking views of the river and the surrounding forest are well worth the effort. Additionally, there are historical sites, including an old mill, that can be observed along the trail.

trailData.name: Amicalola Falls to Len Foote Hike Inn
trailData.description:
This is a one-way hike to the Len Foote Hike Inn. This unique, secluded retreat is tucked away in the mountains and only accessible by foot. More information and reservation bookings can be found at http://hike-inn.com/

The trail begins at the Amicalola Falls State Park parking area, travels through the lush forest and past the falls, and ends at the Len Foote Hike Inn.

trailData.name: Pine Mountain East and West Loop Trail
trailData.description: This trail starts at the parking lot off Komatsu Drive and leads to the summit of Pine Mountain, the highest point in the City of Cartersville. Be prepared for a rugged and challenging hike with steep sections and exposed tree roots—sturdy footwear is recommended. Your effort will be rewarded with stunning views of Atlanta and the surrounding metropolitan area.

trailData.name: Arabia Mountain, Klondike, and Forest Trails Loop
trailData.description: The trail has several beautiful arched granite bridges, a wooden boardwalk, and a short segment over a rock outcropping. Most of the trail is on a paved greenway, which makes it perfect for beginners. There is a slight incline to get up the mountain, but it's mostly shady along the way. However, once you reach the peak, the trail markers disappear, making it a bit challenging to find the trail.

trailData.name: Amicalola Falls Loop
trailData.description:
The hike through the picturesque trail offers breathtaking views of the waterfall that are truly unparalleled. The well-maintained trails and clear markings make it easy for hikers to navigate, providing a seamless outdoor experience. 

The climb to the top is strenuous, with 425 stairs that help you gain elevation. Visitors will find restroom facilities conveniently located at the large trailhead/visitor center parking area.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Glen Falls Trail
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Tennessee
trailData.description:
This is an excellent short hike with many beautiful natural sights. The trail leads through a beautiful forest and visits several small waterfalls and flowing creeks. 

Once you reach the bridge, walk about 50' further and take the stone stairs to your right. You will pass through a stone door in the rock. Coming out of the rock, you will be overlooking the bridge. Continue alongside the creek for about another 1/4 mile. You will pass several small cascades (when it's recently rained), and...

trailData.name: East Palisades North Loop
trailData.description:
The East Palisades North Loop has ascending and descending trails, with some steep areas. The trails are shady, well-marked, and well-maintained. The trail eventually led to a secret bamboo forest beside the river, passing stunning streams and enormous rock formations. There are many peaceful places to observe people gliding down the river in kayaks and tubes. 

While strolling along the Chattahoochee River, you can explore the bamboo forest and look from the observation deck. Picnics are...

trailData.name: East Palisades, North Loop and Bamboo Forest
trailData.description: This route maximizes the property with minimal retracing. The bamboo forest out and back spur contains most of the retracing, but it is worth the trip.

trailData.name: Sweetwater Creek Red and White Trail Loop
trailData.description: The route starts on the White Trail and winds all the way around to Jack's Hill, then circles around to the waterfall, and back up to the Ruins on the Red Trail back to the trailhead.

trailData.name: Preachers Rock from Woody Gap Recreational Area
trailData.description: A wonderful hike in Georgia's mountains awaits at Preachers Rock, starting from the well-known Woody Gap Recreational Area. This popular trail segment is part of the famous Appalachian Trail and leads to a stunning, wide-open view that will take your breath away. Your journey, though not too long, winds uphill through a beautiful Southern Appalachian forest. You'll walk among tall hardwood trees like oaks and hickories. Depending on the season, especially in late spring or early summer, you...

trailData.name: Big Cedar Mountain and Granny Top via Appalachian Trail
trailData.description:
In the late 1800s, "Bear" Joe Lunsford was a farmer and preacher in the Suches area. He'd climb to a rocky outcrop on what's now the Appalachian Trail to practice his sermons. The view is incredible, and today it's only a half-hour's walk off the pavement.

The Appalachian Trail crosses the highway here. Follow the trail Northbound (where the restrooms are) towards Neil's Gap and Blood Mountain. Look for the trail markers: white rectangles 2" wide by 6" high. These are known as "white...

trailData.name: Kennesaw Mountain Overlook via Little Kennesaw and Brumby Camp
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
This trail begins and ends at the Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park Visitor Center and winds through the forest to the Kennesaw Mountain Overlook. It's a very popular hiking and running trail near Atlanta.

The trail follows the Confederate battle lines and includes well-preserved trenches that are still visible today. Along the path, informative plaques offer historical insights. The path is well-maintained, but be prepared for many rocks and steep inclines that can be slippery;...

trailData.name: Sweetwater Creek White Trail Loop
trailData.description: The trail begins next to the Sweetwater Creek Visitor Center and features Jack's Lake, Sweetwater Creek, and stunning waterfalls. The majority of the trail is covered by dense forest. The views along the trail and the rapids are spectacular. The terrain is well-maintained with a mix of narrow and flat sections. There are also some steep hills and rocky areas.

trailData.name: Sitton's Gulch Trail
trailData.description: This route features a steady descent into the gorge and then parallels Sitton Gulch Creek to the edge of the park boundary. Save some energy, as the way back will require some uphill hiking at the end. Along the way, there are beautiful creek and waterfall views. This is a nice and shaded hike through a scenic forest which makes for an excellent choice in the summer to cool off.

trailData.name: Pine Log Creek Trail
trailData.description: This trail starts at the parking lot off State Route 140 and winds through a shaded forest with interesting rock formations, passing a quarry and following along Pine Log Creek with beautiful water views. Be prepared for steep parts and narrow sections. Along the way, you’ll find benches to sit, relax, and enjoy the serene atmosphere.

trailData.name: Dukes Creek Trail
trailData.description:
There is a parking fee at this trailhead unless you have a Forest Service Pass. State Park passes are not accepted.
 
From the parking lot, the trail heads down a series of stairs and follows an old roadbed. There are wooden boardwalks and stairs occasionally along the way. Most of the trail is wide and flat with switchbacks. 

As you wind your way down to the bottom of the ravine, you can hear the occasional sounds of the waterfalls. The first sizable falls are viewed from the trail. The...

trailData.name: Fall Creek Waterfall
trailData.location_label: Dawson Forest Wildlife Management Area, Georgia

trailData.name: Indian Seats Loop
trailData.description: The Indian Seats Trail is nestled within the beautiful Sawnee Mountain Preserve and winds through various ecosystems, showcasing the region's diverse flora and fauna. Along the way, hikers will travel through serene woodlands with the occasional glimpse of wildlife. The highlight of the trail is the Indian Seats rock formation, providing breathtaking panoramic views.

trailData.name: Amicalola Falls Lookout via Creek Trail and West Ridge Falls Access
trailData.description:
The hike takes you to Amicalola Falls, a 729-foot, Georgia's tallest waterfall. The trail winds through hardwood forest and begins on the Creek Trail, which runs alongside a flowing creek. As you continue along the creek, you'll soon come to a set of steps that leads to the Reflection Pool and your first view of Amicalola Falls. From here, you'll climb more than 175 steps to reach a bridge that spans the base of the falls and offers a breathtaking vista.

Once you pass the base of the falls,...

trailData.name: Blood Mountain via Appalachian Trail
trailData.description:
This is a glorious and challenging hike to the summit of Blood Mountain following the Appalachian Trail. The trail offers varied terrain with some smooth sections leading to more technical rocky parts. 

As you navigate the trail, there are several peaceful spots to enjoy nature and the stunning views. To reach the summit, follow the white markings. Once at the summit continue a little further to reach the Blood Mountain AT Shelter. Parking is available at Neels Gap.

trailData.name: Allatoona Falls Trail
trailData.description:
The Allatoona Falls Trail is breathtaking, close to Toonigh Creek's mouth into Lake Allatoona. The falls, also called Toonigh Creek Falls and Allatoona Falls, were formerly known as Hause Shoals. 

The trail begins at the trailhead, crosses the Little River bridge, and then crosses an overpass to reach a section used for sand dredging. From there, it follows the river's narrow channel until it rises to a cliff between Lake Allatoona. Lovely wildflowers dot the trail.
 
The river, waterfall,...

trailData.name: Little River Canyon
trailData.location_label: Little River Canyon National Preserve, Alabama
trailData.description: This is an amazing hiking trail featuring stunning waterfalls, canyon rims, and sandstone cliffs. However, please note that the trail can be quite rocky and steep in some parts, especially along the stairs. Additionally, the water levels and waterfall itself may vary depending on the season, with the best views typically available during the spring and summer months. If you're looking to cool off after your hike, there's also a beautiful swimming hole nearby.

trailData.name: Sweetwater Creek Yellow Trail
trailData.description:
Explore the beautiful shores of Sweetwater Creek on this popular trail located not too far from Atlanta. The Sweetwater Creek Yellow Trail features a large steel and wood span bridge leading over to the eastern side of the creek, where hikers can explore the rocky outcrops and see the ruins of the New Manchester Mill from the Civil War era. 

Visitors will be rewarded with some far-reaching views of the Atlanta skyline after tackling the climb through the young forest after the bridge....

trailData.name: Amicalola Falls
trailData.description: As the tallest cascading waterfall in the Southeast, Amicalola Falls offers breathtaking views and an impressive water display as it tumbles down the rocks. Visitors can explore the area via staircases that lead to various viewpoints, providing beautiful close-up views of the waterfall and its surrounding beauty. Be cautious, as some sections can be slippery, especially near the waterfall.

trailData.name: Sope Creek Loop from Paper Mill Road
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: This route begins at the Sope Creek Parking Area and begins along a wide and flat trail past a scenic little lake. The trail travels through a beautiful hardwood forest with rolling hills and bubbling streams. There are many other interconnected trails in this extensive network to shorten or extend your route.

trailData.name: Cartecay River Loop Trail
trailData.location_label: Rich Mountain Wildlife Management Area, Georgia
trailData.description: This incredible trail runs alongside the river for a large portion of the route. Most of the trail is an easy hike along a flat surface. There are a few places with steep elevation changes to be aware of. After rainfall, the rocks can be slippery and challenging to navigate. There are several places to stop along the river and rest or enjoy river views.

trailData.name: West Trail: Pigeon Hill to Kennesaw Mountain Visitor Center
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
The West Trail connects Pigeon Hill to the Kennesaw Mountain Visitor Center and provides a hike through significant Civil War sites in the Kennesaw Mountain area. This hike alternates between rough and smooth gravel trails.  

After crossing Pigeon Hill, the trail climbs Little Kennesaw Mountain's rugged backside. A great place to sit and take in the sights of the southern sky is to get off the track and climb uphill to one of the massive rocks. An interpretive sign and three re-creations of...

trailData.name: Klondike Trail to Arabia Mountain
trailData.description:
This is a lovely scenic trail to the summit of Mount Arabia. The trail starts at the parking area off Klondike Road, where parking and restrooms are available.  The route is well-marked throughout, with stone cairns marking the way up and down the mountain. 

The summit has excellent views of the surrounding landscape and is a beautiful sunset spot. Arabia Mountain Park is home to a unique ecosystem with succulents, mosses, diamorphine, pine trees, and much more.

trailData.name: Sweetwater Red and White Loop Trail
trailData.description: The Sweetwater Red and White Loop Trail features peaceful meadows and a tumbling brook. This trail winds along Sweetwater Creek, which is well-known for its breathtaking vistas of rapids and waterfalls. The trail has several staircases and rocky scrambles. The verdant, lush islands scattered along the creek's bed are reflected in the glassy pools of water beside it. Watch out for slick rocks as you go along the trail.

trailData.name: Raven Cliff Falls Trail
trailData.description:
There is an amenities fee per vehicle for trash, bathrooms, picnic table, and parking use at the trailhead. Arrive early as the parking area is limited, and the parking lot fills up fast. The road closes during winter, depending on weather and road conditions. 

The trail follows Dodd Creek over roots and rocks, with excellent views and cool-down opportunities. The Raven Cliff Falls area is a fantastic place to enjoy the water and watch Matthews Creek cascade down Raven Cliff. 

Along the...

trailData.name: Fort Yargo Lake Loop
trailData.description:
This trail is intended for multi-use and is shared by both hikers and mountain bikers. This trail is well-marked and features several connecting paths to extend your hike or bike ride.

If you begin on the Fort side, be aware not to take a left shortly after entering the woods, as this will lead you to the pavilion/party area. Also, be cautious not to turn right mistakenly and end up on the steep bike trail.

trailData.name: Lula Lake Classic Loop
trailData.description:
Reservations are REQUIRED to access this area.

Lula Lake Land Trust is private property and is open on the first and last weekends of each month. Hours and dates vary by season, so check the following site before planning your trip. 

It is open the first and last Saturday and Sunday of each month and there are limited passes available. It is $15 per car for the pass and hikers must buy them online at lulalake.org before arrival.

trailData.name: Tumbling Waters Trail
trailData.description:
This trail offers breathtaking views of the nearby river, falls, and surrounding area. The difficulty level of the trail can range from easy to moderate, depending on the season and recent rainfall. 

The Upper Overlook trail may occasionally be closed for repairs due to severe weather and ongoing remediation. However, the Lower Overlook trail is always open. It runs parallel to the mountain bike trail, so it is essential to follow the foot trail to avoid getting in the way.

trailData.name: High Falls Trail
trailData.description: Please do not walk on the river rocks on the unmarked portion of this trail as they are on private property.

trailData.name: Pine Mountain Summit via East Loop Trail
trailData.description: Mountain biking is permitted on Wednesdays and Saturdays on Backpack & Pocketknife Trail only.

trailData.name: Fall Branch Falls Trail
trailData.description: Short and sweet with a nice little waterfall at the end to enjoy.

trailData.name: Lake Trahlyta Trail
trailData.description: A walking trail around the lake in Vogel State Park. It features an optional side trail down to a viewing platform for the waterfalls on Wolff Creek. There are exceptional views of Blood and Slaughter Mountains.

trailData.name: Cochran Shoals Trail from Interstate North Trailhead
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: If you're looking for a scenic and serene path surrounded by trees and river views, this trail is perfect for you. It is well-maintained and marked, making it easy to navigate for all levels of hikers and mountain bikers. The direction of the trail changes depending on the day, allowing everyone to use it as needed. Please refer to the trailhead signage upon arrival for more information.

trailData.name: Emery Creek Falls Trail
trailData.description: The Emery Creek/Holly Creek Trail is a moderately challenging and beautiful trail that ends with a two-step set of waterfalls. During the journey, your shoes will get wet as you cross the creek eleven times. However, the first crossing is the deepest, so it's best not to attempt it when the water level is high. To help you stay on the trail, look for orange ties or spray paint on rocks and trees, or green rectangles on trees.

trailData.name: Kennesaw Mountain Peak Trail
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: Standing 1,808 above sea level, Big Kennesaw is a prominent monadnock (isolated peak not connected to another chain) in Cobb County, GA. The one-mile hike from the Visitor Center to this point is one of the more popular (and challenging!) trails in the park. Offering commanding views to the north and south, this mountain has been significant for centuries. Native Americans were said to have named it either after a prominent Chief in the area or from the term ‘Ghaneesah’, which meant ‘sacred...

trailData.name: Anna Ruby Falls Trail
trailData.description:
The trail leading to Anna Ruby Falls is only accessible from 9 AM to 4 PM, every day of the week. The path is paved and runs along a stream, offering information plaques about the surrounding area.  

Anna Ruby Falls comprises twin waterfalls that form at the base of the falls by the joining of two separate streams, Curtis Creek and York Creek, which then form Smith Creek and flow into Unicoi Lake. The falls are located on Tray Mountain, Georgia's sixth-highest peak, and Curtis Creek drops...

trailData.name: Kennesaw Mountain and Visitor Center Short Loop
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
At the start of the Kennesaw Mountain and Visitor Center Short Loop, the steep ascent to the summit of Kennesaw Mountain begins. The trail passes through rocky areas. This wooded, shaded trail has stretches of spacious dirt and gravel roads. The path gets more rocky as it climbs.

Throughout the trail, you will encounter wildlife like deer, wild turkeys, squirrels, and snakes. At the summit, you will explore Civil War monuments and artillery honoring the 1864 Atlanta Campaign. Take breaks in...

trailData.name: Laurel Ridge Trail
trailData.description: This beautiful route travels through Buford Dam Park and showcases the natural beauty of this lush forested area. Plenty of shade along the trail makes it an excellent choice for hot summer days. The terrain features rolling hills with several steep but short inclines. This trail is not well marked in some areas, and it is recommended to download the offline map before heading out.

trailData.name: Sope Creek via Cochran Shoals from Interstate North Trailhead
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description:
This longer route along the Chattahoochee River starts at the Interstate North Trailhead on Cochran Shoals. The trail continues north to the Sope Creek area, looping back to the trailhead.

This is a popular mountain biking route.

trailData.name: Sunset Rock via Point Park
trailData.description: From Point Park, follow this route to Sunset Rock, which offers breathtaking views of the Tennessee River and the valley. The trail includes steep metal-grated steps that connect with the Bluff Trail. Along the way, you will find several informational plaques about the area's rich history. It's worth noting that the trail is fully shaded in the morning.

trailData.name: McDaniel Farm Park Trail
trailData.description:
This is a fantastic trail in McDaniel Farm Park. The route is well-maintained and follows spacious paths that wind alongside babbling creeks, picturesque meadows, and serene woods nestled in the heart of the city.

 The majority of the trail is pleasantly shaded and there are two dedicated dog parks, a playground for kids, and convenient amenities such as picnic tables and relaxing bench swings scattered throughout the area.

trailData.name: Wolf Laurel Top via Appalachian Trail
trailData.description:
This trail features a portion of the Appalachian Trail that runs from Tesnatee Gap to the West, over Cow Rock Mountain, and along the ridge line to Wolf Laurel Top. The trail is incredibly scenic, taking you through various terrains and elevations. 

The initial section out of Tesnatee Gap is steep, but it flattens out for a while before there is a moderate climb up Cow Rock Mountain. After this climb, the trail becomes fairly moderate as it traverses the ridge line between Cow Rock and Wolf...

trailData.name: White and Red Trail Loop
trailData.description: This trail at Sweetwater Creek State Park is a fantastic way to explore the area. The journey begins at the Sweetwater Creek Parking Lot and winds along the White Trail through the lush forest. It eventually joins with the Red Trail, taking you past the historic New Manchester Mill Ruins and alongside the tranquil creek. Keep in mind that parking tends to fill up quickly on weekends and holidays, so it's best to arrive early.

trailData.name: Springer Mountain
trailData.description:
This hike will take you to the summit of Springer Mountain, which is the southern terminus of the Appalachian Trail and the Benton Mackaye Trails. It also features a shelter and campsites.

Enjoy stunning vistas at the stop before returning the way you came. 

The trail is not too long, but it is rocky. Parking is limited, so get there early to ensure a spot.

trailData.name: Hemlock Falls Trail
trailData.description: The trail leading to Hemlock Falls is straightforward and an easy hike, but the path beyond that, up to Upper Moccasin Creek Falls, is rugged and challenging. There are several cascades to see along the way, and the trail passes through a beautiful forested area that provides ample shade. However, there are some rocky sections along the way, so it's essential to maintain good footing while hiking.

trailData.name: Unicoi Lake Loop
trailData.description:
This wonderful family-friendly trail takes visitors on a loop around the scenic Lake Unicoi. Perfect for a quick and easy walk, this pleasant route is relatively flat and shaded the whole way. 

There are many good fishing spots and docks along the way, as well as a playground. There is one short section where you'll have to walk along the road at the dam.

trailData.name: Bear Hair Gap Trail
trailData.description: The hike starts by cabin #7 and wanders through a beautiful forest. There are several refreshing creek crossings to cool down in. After the hike, there are plenty of picnic tables to rest and enjoy. The trail is in good condition, with a few steep climbs that offer a great workout. However, the effort is worth it as there is a beautiful overlook at the top.

trailData.name: Chattahoochee River Loop from Interstate North Trailhead
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia

trailData.name: Lake Zwerner (aka Yahoola Creek Reservoir)
trailData.description:
Lake Zwerner Trail is a looping trail around the Yahoola Creek Reservoir at the outskirts of Dahlonega GA. Beautiful lake & amazing mountain views. The trail twists & turns around the lake & through the woods

Lake Zwerner Trail is a good challenge for the casual hiker.  The scenery is amazing.  There are some challenging areas where the trail gets steep (50%). But to break up the hike, there are several benches, a couple of picnic areas, and two swings benches. The trail between the two...

trailData.name: Miller Gap to Preacher's Rock via the Appalachian Trail
trailData.description: Sections of this trail are not maintained so may be difficult to follow. Be sure to follow your location on the AllTrails app to prevent getting lost.

trailData.area_name: Vickery Creek Unit- Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area
trailData.name: Vickery Creek From Oxbo Road
trailData.location_label: Vickery Creek Unit- Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: The trail begins at Oxbo Trail Parking and takes you on the Vickery Creek Trail and Oxbo Trail. Along the trail, you will be surrounded by thick forests and lush greenery. This trail features well-marked paths and waterfalls along the Big Creek. Some sections of the route are rocky and steep. Keep an eye out for the protruding roots on the ground.

trailData.name: Smith Creek Trail to Anna Ruby Falls
trailData.description:
The trail leads through a lush forest to the gorgeous Anna Ruby Falls. The ascent to the ridge is steady and may leave your heart pounding, but the footing is good and the trail is well-marked.

Be prepared to cross several creeks along the way, and wear shoes that can get wet. In the summer months, you may encounter overgrown sections and fallen trees.

trailData.name: Ramrock Mountain via Appalachian Trail
trailData.description: This section of the Appalachian Trail stretches from Woody Gap to Ramrock Mountain. It's a relatively easy hike that lies to the west of Woody Gap. Along the trail, you'll find several campsites where hikers can rest and enjoy the picturesque views. However, the top of the trail only offers stunning views to the south.

trailData.name: Pine Mountain Summit via West Loop
trailData.description: There are two loops that connect to Pine Mountain - the East Loop and the West Loop. This route follows along the West Loop on a rugged and challenging hike that reaches 1,562 feet above sea level. Once you reach the top of this mountain, you will be at the highest point in the City of Cartersville.

trailData.name: Stone Wall, Stone Tower, and West Overlook Trails Loop
trailData.description:
The stunning rock formations and the mesmerizing views are truly remarkable. Stone Wall Tower Overlook is beautiful and offers an excellent spot to relax. 

The area is perfect for enjoying the views and catching the sunrise or sunset. The trail gets relatively narrow in some areas and includes metal grate stairs, lots of rocks, and roots. During fall, the path is covered in leaves, sometimes making it slippery.

There is a parking fee at the trailhead, and restrooms are accessible.

trailData.name: Long Branch Loop Trail
trailData.description: This is a well-maintained and peaceful route that is great for the whole family.  The sound of the water makes for a very relaxing atmosphere. The road up to the parking lot may be eroded, so high-clearance vehicles are suggested. The trail itself is wide and shady, making it perfect for escaping the summer heat.

trailData.name: High Shoals Falls Trail
trailData.description:
To access this trailhead, there is a 1.25-mile long, rough, narrow gravel road that might be challenging for those unaccustomed to driving on rough terrain.
This trail begins with a gentle climb through a dense forest, surrounded by the soothing sounds of the creek. As you hike deeper into the woods, the path becomes more rugged. The highlight of the route is the falls themselves, which cascade over 80 feet into a rocky pool below. There is another waterfall just a short way past High Shoals...

trailData.name: Three Forks and Springer Mountain via Appalachian Trail
trailData.description:
This strenuous but rewarding hike through the Blue Ridge Wildlife Management Area can be done as a lengthy day hike or split up as a backpacking trip with one of the campsites along the way. 

The trail is well-maintained, but a few areas are not well-marked, so be sure to stay alert and keep an eye on the amp. The highlight of the trail is the spectacular view from the summit of Springer Mountain on a clear day.

trailData.name: Desoto Falls Bottom and Ice Cave
trailData.description: This is a lovely short hike with spectacular views of Desoto Falls. The accompanying swimming hole provides a nice place to cool down on a hot summer day. The trail begins from the parking lot on County Road 613. It descends steeply to West Fork Little River, meandering alongside it until it reaches DeSoto Falls. The trail surface is rocky, with roots in some parts, so watch your footing.

trailData.name: West Palisades Trail
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: This is a serene hike that passes through a stunning forest and runs alongside a river. The trail is clearly marked and can be rocky in some parts. The route has undulating hills that can be a little challenging, but they make for an excellent workout. The terrain is mostly natural and has wide areas to tread on. There are numerous fantastic spots by the water where you can stop, have a snack or lunch, and enjoy the scenery.

trailData.name: Cheatham Hill Trail
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: Dirt or wide crushed gravel tracks throughout. Open meadows along Old John Ward Road, wooded hills along Hardage Mill trail. Winding creeks babbling over rock and gravel along Hardage Mill trail.

trailData.name: Kennesaw Mountain
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia

trailData.name: Benton MacKaye, Owen's Overlook, and Appalachian Trail Loop
trailData.description: This trail is well-marked and offers a scenic view throughout the journey. The path has several ups and downs as it winds through the rolling hills of a beautiful forest. Although the trail does not lead to the summit of Springer Mountain, you can choose to take a short spur trail to the top to add a little extra distance. You will follow white blazes on the Benton MacKaye Trail (BMT) and Appalachian Trail (AT).

trailData.name: Long Creek Falls via Appalachian and Benton MacKaye Trail
trailData.description:
The starting point of the trail can be found on a rough path off the main road. It is advisable to drive with caution, with 4x4 vehicles recommended. At the beginning of the hike, you will be walking very close to the creek along a wide gravel path. Gradually, you will move away from the creek and the path will become more natural, with roots and rocks. 

There are several small paths branching off from the main trail that lead to creekside campsites. You will hear numerous waterfalls along...

trailData.area_name: Vickery Creek Unit- Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area
trailData.name: Vickery Creek Trail Short Loop
trailData.location_label: Vickery Creek Unit- Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description:
The Vickery Creek Trail, accessible from Riverside Road, offers a scenic journey alongside the creek. The trail meanders through a rolling forest, showcasing the lush, young, ferny landscape. Walking along the creek's north bank, you can relax and enjoy the serene beauty of the falls, keeping an eye out for wildlife such as herons and geese.

One of the highlights of the trail is the Roswell Mill waterfall. There are areas on both sides of the water where you can carefully scramble down the...

trailData.name: Frosty Mountain via Appalachian Approach Trail
trailData.description:
Frosty Mountain is located in the Chattahoochee National Forest along the Approach Trail to Springer Mountain (the southern terminus of the Appalachian Trail.) 

The summit was once the site of a U.S. Forest Service lookout tower, but it has been removed and all that remains is a flat area suitable for overnight camping. A seasonal spring is located a short distance to the southeast although it may be difficult to find especially in the summer months. 

If you continue further past Frosty...

trailData.name: Henderson Park Loop
trailData.description:
Henderson Park offers diverse attractions, making it a fantastic place to explore. The park features a beautiful lake, a pond teeming with fish, turtles, frogs, and tadpoles, and a marsh area with excellent dock spaces.

Visitors can use the ball fields, multiple bathrooms with water fountains, and two playground areas. The park also boasts a butterfly garden brimming with wildlife. The trail encompasses a mix of wooded singletrack and paved surfaces and a lovely waterfall with a spectacular...

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Sunset Rock via Craven's House Trail
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Tennessee
trailData.description:
The trail to Sunset Rock, beginning near the historic Cravens House, provides a rewarding hike to one of Lookout Mountain's best viewpoints, offering both a walk through history and stunning scenery. The Cravens House, built before the Civil War, witnessed famous battles, and starting your hike here adds a special touch. The trail itself will take you over some rugged, rocky ground and includes sections with stone steps, making for an interesting trek.

Your destination, Sunset Rock, is a...

trailData.name: Amadahy Loop
trailData.description: The trail is marvelous and easy to navigate. It offers fantastic views of the water and is nicely shaded. There are plenty of swimming spots along the way. About halfway through, there’s a spur trail to the point with plenty of picnic tables, ideal for lunch or a snack. Remember to bring bug repellent in the warmer months.

trailData.name: Walk-in Campsites to Sitton's Gulch Trail
trailData.description: Hike from the walk-in campsites trail (white) through grassy meadows to the West Rim Loop trail (yellow) all the way down to Sitton’s Gulch Trail (black).  Features shaded hiking, bridge crossings, rock formations, stairs, river and waterfalls.

trailData.name: Lake Blue Ridge Loop
trailData.location_label: Blue Ridge Lake Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description:
This wooded trail has nice views of the lake, but can be narrow in places. You may want sturdy shoes for this trail as there are uneven sections with rocks and roots.

Users have suggested that for hikers when you are in the parking lot, don’t look at the sign for the bikes because it points you the wrong way. If you are looking at the lake, walk to the far left and it starts on a very small boardwalk.

trailData.name: Appalachian Trail: Tesnatee Gap to Cow Rock Mountain
trailData.description:
The trail starts at Tesnatee Gap and climbs steeply uphill through a canopy of young hardwood trees that provide shade. It is bordered by brightly colored wildflowers and winds through a rocky woodland with ferns and green underbrush. As you climb, the trail meanders through narrow switchbacks, eventually opening up breathtaking views of the surrounding peaks and valleys. The ascent gets steeper as the woodland gives way to more rocky ground.

When you reach the top of Cowrock Mountain, you...

trailData.name: Little Kennesaw Mountain
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia

trailData.name: Leita Thompson Memorial Park Trail
trailData.description:
This is a lovely well maintained gravel loop. It includes a pond and nine bridges crisscrossing a brook and through the woods. 

Accessibility: Visitors using wheelchairs, mobility equipment, or strollers may need all-terrain tires or adaptive/motorized equipment for the surface type and grade. Visitors using wheelchairs, mobility equipment, or strollers may need assistance in the steeper sections or to avoid them for safety.

Accessible Parking:
Number of designated accessible spaces: 1 at...

trailData.name: West Rim Loop Trail
trailData.description: This rugged trail explores part of Cloudland Canyon State Park and offers many stunning views of the canyon. Beginning from the small parking lot off Cloudland Canyon Park Road, you'll follow the West Rim Loop Trail. The forests here are home to a wide variety of wildlife, such as deer, turkeys, raccoons, red-tail hawks, and foxes. The rugged dirt terrain is rocky and muddy in parts, so wearing sturdy hiking shoes is a good idea.

trailData.name: Laurel Falls and Lost Falls Trails Loop
trailData.description: This trail starts counter-clockwise on the orange blazed trail, going southwest. Eventually reaching Lost Falls, the hiker turns left and continues back northeast on the blue blazed trail, back to the parking area.

trailData.name: Stanley Gap and Benton Mackaye Loop Trail
trailData.description: Stanley Gap is a multi-use trail so keep an eye out for mountain bikers. The trail maintenance is excellent. The parking lot for the falls fills up early and if it is rutted, you can follow the gravel road to another lot closer to the falls.

trailData.name: Blood Mountain Loop via Slaughter Creek Trail
trailData.description: Parking is located right at the southern end of Lake Winfield Scott. There is a 2nd parking lot closer to the trailhead that is accessed through the main park entrance.

trailData.name: Settles Bridge Park Extended Loop Trail
trailData.description:
The first quarter of this travel is a nice wide paved multi-purpose trail. After that, it drops off into a varying mix of dirt, gravel, or some kind of tarp over gravel. Once you're into the woods on the dirt trail it becomes a wonderful trail that feels far more remote than it really is. 

There is some trail finding difficulty at a few points. It's somewhat flat with lots of space between the trees so it seems like there could be many trails.

trailData.name: Suwanee Greenway to Ivy Creek Greenway
trailData.description: Explore the Suwanee Creek Greenway and the Ivy Creek Greenway on this lengthy but primarily flat trail through the peaceful forest. The terrain is a mix of wooden walkways and pavement. The wooden sections can get slippery after rain, so take care, especially if you're on a bike ride. The trail is well-signposted and shaded the entire length. There are bathrooms available on both ends.

trailData.name: Brasstown Bald Trail
trailData.description:
This is a steep but scenic walk to Brasstown Bald Visitors Center and viewpoint.

Although this trail is paved, most is over a 12% grade, and there are some sharp switchbacks, and it would be very steep for manual wheelchair and stroller users.

The distance from the lower parking lot (Jacks Gap) to the Visitor's Center and back is 7 miles. Visitors can also drive to the Upper Parking Lot and make it a shorter half-mile jaunt. However, the road to the higher portion may be closed in winter....

trailData.name: Project Chimps Yellow Trail
trailData.description: If you want a good workout, take your time and explore the Yellow Trail. Several switchbacks help mitigate the incline as you hike to the top of Paris Mountain. When the trees are not in full bloom, you can see directly into the Peachtree Habitat where chimpanzees live in sanctuary. A section of this trail is on a gravel service road; a future addition will move the trail fully into the woods. A $2 day use fee is requested in the parking lots before you start hiking.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Glenn Falls via St. Elmo Trail
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Tennessee
trailData.description: This route begins at the St. Elmo playground, and travels along the Guild Trail until it connects with the St. Elmo Trail. The trail goes straight up through several short switchbacks until you start heading south where it meets with Glenn Falls Trail a little over a quarter mile from the parking area.

trailData.name: Nottely Reservoir Trail
trailData.description: This is a great little trail with stoping points and rest benches with beautiful views of the lake. A few steady inclines on the Orange Trail but it is shaded. There are also quite a few spots to jump in the water for a swim if you desire! Everyone should bring water on this hike and if you plan on jumping in the water at the lake bring a towel!

trailData.name: Marble Mine Trail to Upper Lake Loop
trailData.location_label: James H. (Sloppy) Floyd State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: The loop trail takes you to James H. Floyd State Park. It’s well-marked and well-shaded but be prepared for steep sections at the beginning. Bring bug spray to protect against mosquitoes. Along the way, you will find a marble mine cave with a small waterfall trickle. There are also picnic tables, a fishing area, and kayak rentals available. Parking is available at the trailhead.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Cravens House Loop Trail
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Tennessee
trailData.description: Begin this adventure at the historic Craven's House. Take the main path and then turn right onto "Rifle Pits Trail" at the first split. After that, turn left onto "Upper Truck Trail". Here, you can explore the remnants of the old CCC Camp Demaray that housed 200 men. Continue left, and at the next intersection, turn left onto "Gum Spring Trail". This is the roughest part of the trail that will lead you to Sunset Rock. Finally, take a left onto "Craven's House Trail" to get back to your...

trailData.name: Homestead Trail, Sweet Gum Trail, Osprey Loop Trail and Lakeside Trail
trailData.location_label: Red Top Mountain State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This loop trail starts from the parking lot at the end of Lodge Road Southeast and leads into Red Top Mountain State Park. It winds through the shaded forest, offering beautiful views of Lake Allatoona. Be prepared for rocky sections and exposed tree roots along the way—sturdy footwear is recommended.

trailData.name: Cascade Springs Nature Preserve Outer Loop
trailData.description:
This lovely wooded trail is a fantastic way to explore Cascade Springs Nature Preserve.  The trailhead can be accessed via Cascade Road, where you'll find a large parking lot. 

The route is marked, but there are lots of intersecting trails, so keep an eye on the map to make sure you are on the right path. The trail follows a wide paved path before traveling along a narrower footpath. The area feels far removed from the city and makes for a perfect nature escape.

trailData.name: West Overlook Trail
trailData.description:
Fort Mountain State Park is filled with horse trails, biking trails, walking trails, camping sites, and a lake. Once you arrive at the park you'll pay the entrance fee and will receive a park map.

Start on the West Overlook Trail and come back down the CCC Tower Trail. This is a 1 mile trail great for anyone of all ages. You start off at 2,650 ft. of elevation and gain 200 ft. of elevation during the trail. The West Overlook trail is 0.5 miles long that takes you straight to the overlook....

trailData.name: Flat Creek Loop
trailData.description: This trail is well-maintained and offers a peaceful experience as you make your way through the forest, listening to the sound of the creek and small waterfalls. However, the terrain can be challenging due to rocks and roots, especially when the ground is wet. There are a few uphill sections, but it's still a pleasant hike, and it's also dog-friendly.

trailData.name: Doll's Head Trail
trailData.description: The boardwalk over the lake is beautiful. The doll head art installation is interesting.

trailData.name: Chattahoochee River Trail from Columns Drive
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description:
The Chattahoochee River Trail follows the Chattahoochee River, where you can see lots of waterfowl soaring in the skies above and take in views of angular rock shoals. The landscape transitions between gentler and rocky areas, which can get muddy after rain.

The trail passes through beautiful wetlands and woodlands with hilly sections as it goes on. There are several spots along the trail where you can stop and take in breathtaking views of the surrounding area from rocky bluff overlooks.

trailData.name: Unicoi to Helen Trail
trailData.description:
This hiking trail starts from the lodge and follows a picturesque path through the woodlands of Unicoi State Park. Once you complete your hike, you can easily visit many restaurants or go shopping in Helen.

If you choose to hike this trail from the town of Helen, you can do so without paying any fees. There is a convenient free parking lot available at the trailhead in Helen.

trailData.name: Cochran Mill Loop 1 and 2 (Orange)
trailData.description:
Cochran Mill Park takes you through a setting rich in historical and natural characteristics. The park features beautiful waterfalls, enormous boulders, rock outcrops, wildflowers, native azaleas, and mountain laurels.

The trail goes through the forest and includes several hills. Along the trail, you may encounter wildlife like deer and snakes. There are some shaded and exposed areas. The trail is rocky and steep in places, so you'll need to be careful where you hike.

trailData.name: Kennesaw Mountain via Noonday Creek Trail
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
This lovely trail leads hikers along the Noonday Creek Trail and up to the summit of Kennesaw Mountain. The panoramic views from the top are incredible. To the south, you'll be able to see the whole Atlanta Metro Area, with skylines from downtown to Midtown to Buckhead and Smyrna in the foreground. To the east, you can see all the way to Stone Mountain and the beginnings of the Blue Ridge Mountains to the north and west.

The trail is consistent uphill after a short flat stretch at the start....

trailData.name: Clear Creek to Cartecay River
trailData.location_label: Rich Mountain Wildlife Management Area, Georgia
trailData.description:
Easy to moderate hike on state wildlife lands. Two trails yellow and orange. Take the yellow to the orange and go left or right to end up at some nice falls on the rivers.

A Georgia hunting or fishing license is needed to recreate on state wildlife management areas. For more information on licenses please visit: https://georgiawildlife.com/licenses-permits-passes/choose

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Point Park and Craven's House Loop
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
This well-shaded and well-marked trail features stunning views of Chattanooga, Moccasin Bend, the city, the water, and the surrounding mountain range.

It's particularly lovely at Point Park, where you can learn about the history of the battles that took place there during the Civil War. Be prepared for a path that includes roots and rocks throughout the hike.

trailData.name: Hilltop, Mountainside and Ridgeline Loop
trailData.description: Overall a good family hike with nice city overlooks. It can be rocky.

trailData.name: Len Foote Hike Inn to Amicalola Falls via Appalachian Approach Trail
trailData.description: This hike starts at the Len Foote Hike Inn. This unique, secluded retreat is only accessible on foot. Note that you cannot drive to the start point for this trail. Selecting the "Directions" button on this page will not take you to this starting point. For more information about the inn and reservations, please visit their website: www.hike-inn.com

trailData.name: Cascades and Mill Road Trail
trailData.description: This is a beautiful trail in Cochran Mill Park. It meanders along lovely shaded trails, passing by waterfalls, creeks, and wildlife. The trail begins from Upper Wooten Road, where parking is available. Some sections of the trail can get quite muddy after rain. Take care when walking on rocks around the waterfalls and creeks, as they can be very slippery.

trailData.name: Bowmans Island Trail
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: Dogs are allowed here, but not in the lower pool section by the dam. The dam area is Army Corps Park, and it is not pet friendly. Park at the first lot on the right after the entrance which is the trailhead if you have a dog.

trailData.name: Big Creek Greenway Trail: Roswell to Alpharetta
trailData.description:
Peaceful, family-friendly, wide, paved walk that follows Big Creek with lots of shade.

Accessibility: This trail starts in a paved parking lot on the south end that has designated accessible parking spaces and multiple striped access aisles. The trail surface is smoothly paved and it is typically at least six feet wide. It is mostly gentle, estimated to be 5% or less, except for the last tenth of a mile which is steep.

trailData.name: Sweetwater Creek White and Green Loop
trailData.description: This is a great route to catch the highlights of a great state park.  It takes you through some of the deeper woods with great chances to see wildlife, and the last leg is along the creek itself with views of the rapids and the biggest attraction in the park, the Civil War ruins.
