There are some steeper hills on the Green section but nothing too strenuous.

trailData.name: Charleston Park Trail
trailData.description: This trail is easy to follow and passes through beautiful wooded terrain. It is also suitable for cycling. The directions for cyclists and hikers are clearly marked. There are many ups and downs and sharp turns, which makes it a favorite for cyclists. The best part of this trail is the stunning views of the lake on the outer loop trail. Additionally, there is ample parking available near the trailhead.

trailData.name: Ravine and West Meadow Loop
trailData.description:
This is a scenic hike through Little Mulberry Park. The trail features plenty of elevation changes, with switchbacks to help with the final incline. There is a good mix of shade and exposed areas along the way. Bring plenty of water and sun protection. 

The trails are marked and maintained well, with some paved surfaces and several non-paved offshoots to explore. The view at the bottom of the ravine is the highlight of this route.

trailData.name: Bear Hair Gap Trail to Outlook
trailData.description:
This trail is well-shaded throughout and features beautiful creeks, big rocks, and boulders. The beginning of the hike meanders alongside a creek. For the first half, it's all uphill and a good workout, followed by a steady descent back to the parking lot.

Along the gravel path, there are many rocks and roots to navigate and a few small streams to cross over. The view from the top is obstructed by overgrowth of trees. The trails are not clearly marked, so keep an eye on the map.

trailData.name: Cochran Mill Red Loop
trailData.description: Single track trail shared between hikers and bikers. Signs at the trailhead indicate that bikes should yield to hikers. Please share the trail respectfully.

trailData.name: Mountain View Trail Loop
trailData.description:
The trail passes through vast expanses of rock and shaded woodlands. As you proceed, you'll pass through fields that are golden and lush. Huge, concreted rock cairns lead the trail across vast stretches of bare granite, winding around vegetation-filled patches and puddles. 

The trail offers views of the lake's smooth surface at intervals as it follows the contour of the lakeshore. When the treeline opens up, you'll be rewarded with breathtaking views of the lake reflecting the mountain. The...

trailData.name: Pigeon Hill Loop
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
The Pigeon Hill Loop begins with a broad gravel and dirt trail that gradually ascends. As you proceed, the trail becomes increasingly rocky and steeper as you climb the mountain. An observation platform near the summit of Kennesaw Mountain offers a stunning vista.

As you continue, the trail descends over rocky terrain, with small stones and massive rock steps to navigate. After winding through an open woodland, you'll reach the bare granite top. Hikers can enjoy views of the Black Mountains...

trailData.name: Hardage Mill and Noses Creek Loop
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
This fantastic hike explores the Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park and follows along historical battle lines. The trail is dotted with informative signage on the history of the area.

There are gentle hills rolling through the beautiful forest and wide trails that are well-maintained. The parking lot on Burnt Hickory Road can fill up quickly on the weekends.

trailData.name: Cherokee Bluffs
trailData.description: The rolling meadows, streams, natural shoals, and plethora of local wildlife may be found in Cherokee Bluffs. In addition, there are numerous historic sites for visitors to explore. The park is well-equipped with features, such as a dog park, multipurpose bike and pedestrian walking pathways, a pavilion, an amphitheater, and a playground. The wooden pathways and steps are shady and clearly marked. There are several huge rocks along the trail that make for great climbing opportunities.

trailData.name: Indian Seats, Ridgeline, and Mountainside Trail Loop
trailData.description:
This trail is both beautiful and well maintained, making it clearly marked and accessible for most users. It does include some challenging climbs, but this is mostly a trail for distance instead of inclines. Users also report that this can be a great connector trail to others, so challenges can be added. 

Parts of the Sawnee (mountainside) or mountaintop area may be closed in Winter for construction.

trailData.name: Sweetgum Loop Trail
trailData.location_label: Red Top Mountain State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: Lake Allatoona was built by the Army Corps of Engineers shortly after the end of World War II and it surrounds the park on three sides. This hike on the Homestead Loop is the most varied and interesting in the park.  There are excellent views of Lake Allatoona and the damn from ridges along the trail and this route also drops you down to the shoreline of the lake.  The park has numerous deer and you are likely to see them as you walk the Homestead Loop.

trailData.name: Chattahoochee Pointe Trail
trailData.description:
This park features approximately two miles of gravel surface trails, a disc golf course, and scenic river views.

Accessibility: There is a small gravel parking lot on Chattahoottchee Park Drive by the start of the trail. Users have reported that about half this trail is wheelchair or stroller friendly. The trail surface is gravel and typically at least six feet wide. The grade is mostly gentle (all estimated 5% or less) but heavy-duty or offroad tires may be needed for mobility equipment or...

trailData.name: Lula Falls Trail
trailData.description: This magnificent trail leads to the breathtaking Lula Falls via clear, well-marked paths. It offers an easy gravel trail; if you're up for it, you can scramble down to the waterfall for stunning views.  If you do go down to the falls, make sure you take the New Lula Falls trail instead of the Old Lula Falls trail. The old trail tends to stay damp and slippery due to the mist from the waterfall. You can park at the trailhead on Lula Lake Road.

trailData.name: Kolb's Farm Loop Trail
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This is an enjoyable trail through Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, featuring some lovely views and photo opportunities along the way. The trail itself is nice and wide, with a mix of smooth and gravel terrain. The trail begins and ends at the Cheatham Hill Parking Lot on Cheatham Hill Road.

trailData.name: Coosa Bald
trailData.location_label: Coopers Creek Wildlife Management Area, Georgia

trailData.name: Tribble Mill Trail
trailData.description:
The loop trail around the lake is great, all paved and mostly shaded. Very clean, lots of benches and trash cans. Loads of birds and squirrels. 

Accessibility: There are over 10 designated accessible spaces in the large paved parking lots off of Libsey Lane at the south end of the trail. All of them are van-accessible with striped access aisles. The trail surface is paved (with railings at bridges), and typically at least 6 feet wide. There is a painted dividing line along the trail which...

trailData.name: Old John Ward, Cease Fire, and Kolb Farm Loop
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This route combines the Kolb Farm Loop with the Old John Ward/Cease Fire Trail to create a double loop.

trailData.name: Kennesaw Mountain Overlook via Pigeon Hill Trail
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This trail to the summit of Little Kennesaw Mountain and back is perfect for a quick afternoon workout. There are a few boulders, roots and switchbacks to navigate as you make the relatively constant incline to the top. The views of the Atlanta skyline are a nice reward before heading back via the same route. Paid parking is available at the parking lot on Burnt Hickory Road.

trailData.name: Historic and Tranquil Trails Loop
trailData.description:
This fantastic forested trail in High Falls State Park features lovely switchbacks and superb views of the falls. The trail is mostly shaded, with some rocky and root-filled sections.

The trail has plenty of varied terrain and is steep in sections, making for a wonderful workout. It is also well-marked with informative signs about the wildlife and plants along the way.

trailData.name: Desoto Falls Bottom and Bluff Overlook
trailData.description:
The DeSoto Falls trail is clearly defined, mainly consists of mud and roots, and requires climbing over boulders as you go. The slightly steeper Bluff Trail leads to Icebox Cave and a rainy weather cascade. 

The Bluff Overlook Trail leads to a platform atop a rock cliff that provides an expansive vista of the surrounding limestone cliffs, the Little River, and the Miller Dam, in addition to all the tiers of DeSoto Falls. On a calm day, the river's glassy surface reflects the vibrant sights...

trailData.name: Sawnee Mountain West: Short Loop
trailData.description: This trail combines the Ridgeline Trail and Hilltop Trail for a complete loop around the Sawnee Mountain Preserve. The terrain can be challenging, with decent inclines and a sandy, loose gravel surface. Hiking poles and shoes with good traction are recommended to prevent slipping. There's plenty of shade along the way and plenty of parking at the trailhead.

trailData.name: Yonah Preserve Trails: Creek Trail (Section 200)
trailData.description: This trail starts at the end of Neyelo Road, where you will find a parking lot with restrooms. It then takes you to Yonah Preserve. The trail winds along the shores of Turner Reservoir and through shaded forest. During the spring, there are beautiful wildflowers and butterflies. Be prepared for some roots and rocks along the way—sturdy footwear is recommended.

trailData.name: Helton Creek Falls Trail
trailData.description:
To access this trailhead, you will need to drive on a dirt gravel road that can be a bit rough. Drivers of low-clearance vehicles should proceed with caution.

This short hiking trail will take you to two breathtaking waterfalls and a swimming hole. To enjoy a nice view of the top waterfall, you will need to climb up a few stairs, and then proceed 100 feet further to reach the base of the larger waterfall.

trailData.name: Toccoa Swinging Bridge
trailData.description:
The walk to Toccoa Swing Bridge follows a wide, shaded, and well-marked path. The bridge is the highlight of this trail offering lovely views of the river and a great place to stop and watch the rushing water beneath.

Once you cross the bridge, you will see a small waterfall. The trail is rocky and has lots of roots crossing it.  There are plenty of lovely places to sit and have a picnic at the bridge.

trailData.name: Little Kennesaw Mountain Overlook Via West Trail
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This trail takes you to Little Kennesaw Mountain Overlook via West Trail. It starts with a steep incline through the forest to the summit of Kennesaw Mountain, then continues with a short descent followed by a climb up Little Kennesaw Mountain. The parking area at the trailhead is limited, so it's recommended that you arrive early.

trailData.name: Haw Creek Park Trail
trailData.description:
The Haw Creek Park Trail in Cumming, Georgia, features a mostly shaded, family-friendly environment perfect for hiking and biking. 

Enjoy lovely woodland walking on well-maintained trails, with occasional deer sightings adding to the charm of your adventure. 

This area is also great for picnics in summer months.

trailData.name: Fall Creek Waterfall view
trailData.location_label: Dawson Forest Wildlife Management Area, Georgia

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Sunset Rock Viewpoint
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Tennessee
trailData.description: There's a small parking lot just off the road with 8 spots for compact cars or mid-sized trucks. The trail is made of wide flat stones that create steps.

trailData.name: Hemlock Falls and Moccasin Creek Wildlife Trail
trailData.description: This trail leads hikers through the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest to Hemlock Falls and back again. The trail meanders close to Moccasin Creek for the majority of the journey. There are several beautiful waterfalls to admire, and plenty of good spots to stop and take pictures along the way. The path is relatively wide and not too strenuous, but there are enough rocks, roots, and small elevation changes to keep it interesting.

trailData.name: Silver Comet Trail: Gilmore to Powder Springs
trailData.description:
The Silver Comet Trail travels west through Cobb, Paulding, and Polk counties. This is a paved trail good for walkers, hikers, bicyclists, rollerbladers, horses, and dog walkers. The Silver Comet Trail starts at the Mavell Road Trailhead in Smyrna, Georgia. It ends at the Georgia/Alabama state line, near Cedartown and The Esom Hill Trailhead.

Accessibility: There are 3 designated accessible spaces in the paved parking lot off of Mavell Road at the east end of the trail. All of them are...

trailData.name: Cease Fire Trail
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This trail begins from the parking lot off Burnt Hickory Road and takes you to Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park via the Cease Fire Trail. The parking area at the trailhead is limited, so it's recommended that you arrive early. It’s a lovely hike through a shaded forest with historical battle lines. The trail is well-marked and well-maintained, with informative signage about the area’s history.

trailData.name: Wildcat Creek Trail to Fourth Falls on Fall Creek
trailData.location_label: Dawson Forest Wildlife Management Area, Georgia
trailData.description:
This trail takes you to Fourth Falls via the Wildcat Creek Trail. It winds through the forest alongside Fall Creek. The trail is well-marked and shaded, with the sound of water throughout the hike.

Be prepared for a rough road to access the trailhead – a high-clearance vehicle is recommended. There's a campground and parking available at the trailhead.

trailData.name: Lullwater Loop
trailData.description: Access to Lullwater Preserve is limited to Emory University students, faculty, and employees.	 For more information, please visit https://www.atlantatrails.com/hiking-trails/lullwater-walking-running-trails-emory-university-atlanta

trailData.name: Old John Ward Connector Trail and Cease Fire Trail
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This loop follows the Old John Ward Connector and Cease Fire Trails, taking you to Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park. The trail begins and ends at the Cheatham Hill Parking Lot on Cheatham Hill Road. It offers a good mix of shaded forest areas and sunny meadows and features several Confederate and Union memorials along the way.

trailData.name: Avalanche Trail Loop
trailData.description:
The trails in this area are directional based on the day of the week. If you are hiking or running, please go in the opposite direction of the bikers. 

Mountain bikes have priority on the trails, but foot traffic is welcome too. However, local and SORBA events may cause trail closures. Therefore, it is recommended that you research before planning your day. For the current status of trails, please visit https://www.sorbawoodstock.org/trail-status.

Every dirt trail is composed of loops that...

trailData.name: Appalachian Trail: Three Forks To Hawk Mountain Shelter
trailData.description:
This trail follows a short part of the Appalachian Trail, taking you from Three Forks to Hawk Mountain Shelter. It’s a beautiful hike through the forest with a short detour to see Long Creek Falls.

The trail is well-maintained and easy to follow, but be prepared for roots. There’s a shelter and dispersed camping sites. Parking is available at the trailhead.

trailData.name: Harbins Loop
trailData.description: This peaceful trail through Harbins Park is a great option for beginners. The trail is clean, well-maintained, well-marked, and has relatively smooth terrain throughout. There are gradual elevation changes along the way as you traverse the ridges and ravines of the park. You'll have lovely tree cover most of the way through the woods. There can be lots of leaves, pine straw and sand on the path, which can be slippery.

trailData.name: Ivy Creek Greenway
trailData.description:
The Ivy Creek Greenway is a pleasant and relatively easy walk along the creek. The trail features a mixture of paved and unpaved surfaces and runs underneath a few road bridges.

It's a beautiful wooded trail with not much elevation. It's suitable for hiking, running or mountain biking. There are several connecting side and bike trails if you want to extend your journey. The trail begins at the Gwinnett Environmental and Heritage Center parking lot.

trailData.name: Stanley Gap to Fall Branch Falls via Benton Mackaye Trail
trailData.description: The trail starts at the Stanley Gap parking area and connects to the Benton MacKaye Trail. This is a moderately challenging hike with some elevation changes and a beautiful waterfall at the midway point. You should expect more traffic on the waterfall trail section, as there are multiple access points to the falls. The Stanley Gap and Benton MacKaye portions of the hike are usually less crowded.

trailData.name: Forest and Mile Rock Loop Trail
trailData.description:
Following a dirt trail beneath a shaded forest canopy, the Forest and Mile Rock Loop Trail first passes through towering pines, leafy hardwoods, seasonal wildflowers, mosses, and lichens. The trail then leads out of the woodland into a broad, open granite field where cairns can be seen. This hike section provides insight into Arabia Mountain's quarry history.

As you continue, the trail passes a pond before arriving at a tiny pavilion. Hikers can enjoy views of the treeline on the opposite...

trailData.name: Bob Callan Trail
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: This beautiful trail runs through the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area. The first section follows the Chattahoochee and then Rottenwood Creek upstream, which is relatively flat and shady. After that, you'll make your way up the hillside before coming back down to the creek. The trail is paved the whole way and is great for walking or running, especially after rain, when the other trails in the area might be too muddy.

trailData.name: Sweetwater YOBOY Loop
trailData.description: This is an outstanding hike in Sweetwater Creek State Park. The route follows a combination of the Yellow, Orange, and Blue trails. It winds through beautiful forests and passes Sweetwater Creek. There is varied terrain throughout the journey, with some ups and downs. In spring, visitors can observe the beautiful blooming Rhododendron. Parking, restrooms, and a drinking fountain are available at the start of the trail.

trailData.name: Laurel Ridge Trail Loop
trailData.description:
Smithgall Woods State Park did a great job designing this trail with a breathtaking view of Mount Yonah. This trail offers a pretty scenery with nice mountain overlook at the top. Moderate incline and downhill with roots and some loose gravel, so better with closed toe shoes and maybe a walking stick. 

Parking is $5.

trailData.name: East Mulberry Equestrian Loop
trailData.description: This trail takes you through shaded forests and meadows at Little Mulberry Park. It’s a popular spot for horseback riding and hiking, with benches and picnic tables for resting. Be prepared for steep, rocky sections, roots, stones, and horse droppings along the way. Parking with restrooms is available at the trailhead.

trailData.name: East Palisades
trailData.description:
The steep inclines and rocky sections of the East Palisades trail lead to multiple vistas of the surrounding woodlands and river. One of the trail's attractions is a bamboo forest with 30-foot stalks that produce a calming sound when the wind blows. 

The trail starts upstream alongside the broad river and crosses over on a wooden bridge. The trail passes numerous sizable outcrops of rock as it climbs to a steep bluff overlooking the Chattahoochee River. The riverside trail offers lovely...

trailData.name: Indian Springs Multi-Use Trail [CLOSED]
trailData.description:
This is a beautiful multi-use trail in Indian Springs State Park. The trail runs through a forest alongside Lake McIntosh, but there are limited views of the lake. Once you reach the western end of the lake, you can cut through to a connecting network of trails if you wish to extend your adventure.

The terrain is rocky and features many roots to navigate. There are plenty of ups and downs, which are more suited to experienced mountain bike riders. Watch for birdlife and wildlife, such as...

trailData.name: Bridge Loop
trailData.description:
This trail is designated for for hiking, birding and pedestrian use only. No mountain biking is allowed. 

As of January 1, 2021, dogs and pets are prohibited from all Chicopee Woods Hiking and Mountain Biking Trails, parking areas, and the Elachee Nature Science Center campus. Please see www.elachee.org for updated rules and trail maps.

There is a $5 daily parking fee or you can purchase a $50 annual pass.

trailData.name: Pine Mountain via Coopers Furnace Trail
trailData.description:
This trail takes you to Pine Mountain via Coopers Furnace Trail. It’s a rugged and challenging hike through the forest that climbs to 1,562 feet above sea level.

Once you reach the top, you'll be at the highest point in the City of Cartersville. Wearing comfortable hiking shoes and bringing a hiking stick are recommended for this adventure.

trailData.name: Green Mountain and Toccoa River via Whissenhunt Trail
trailData.description: The trailhead is located on Aska Road, at the Deep Gap Parking Area. You can park your vehicle at the gravel parking lot on the west side of the road and walk across to the Lower Green Mountain Trail. This is a peaceful hike through the forest with several views of the mountains visible through the trees. Several intersecting trails require careful navigation using the map.

trailData.name: Venable Lake Loop
trailData.description:
This trail begins and ends at the parking lot on the corner of Robert E. Lee Boulevard and Stonewall Jackson Drive. From here, you'll make a circuit around Venable Lake, which has plenty of shade for hotter days.

There are beautiful views of Stone Mountain and the lake and informative signs along the way. Sturdy hiking shoes are recommended to help navigate the tree roots, especially after rain when some areas become muddy and slippery.

trailData.name: Rocky Mountain via Appalachian Trail
trailData.description: This trail follows a short section of the Appalachian Trail, starting from the Unicoi Gap Trailhead, where parking is available and leading to the summit of Rocky Mountain. You'll traverse a mostly shaded forest, making the steep climb more comfortable. Your effort will be rewarded with great views of the valley from the summit.

trailData.name: Sweetwater Creek Yellow, Red, and White Loop
trailData.description:
Sweetwater Creek State Park, located just a short distance from downtown Atlanta, boasts over nine miles of hiking trails that showcase the natural and cultural history of the area. The park features Civil War ruins, secluded ponds, and beautiful waterfalls, making it an excellent destination for hikers.

The hike along the creek leads to the ruins of the New Manchester Manufacturing Company, a mill that produced clothing for Confederate troops during the Civil War. The mill was burned down...

trailData.name: Len Foote Inn to Springer Mountain via Appalachian Approach Trail
trailData.description: Hike out and back from Len Foote Inn to Appalachian Trail plaque on Springer Mountain.

trailData.name: Keown Falls Trail
trailData.location_label: Johns Mountain Wildlife Management Area, Georgia
trailData.description:
Hikers recommend doing this trail clockwise. This way, you head up the steep section first and have a more gradual incline in the second half of the hike. This trail begins from the Keown Falls Picnic Area and Trailhead. Here, visitors will find ample parking and a restroom. 

The terrain is rocky with some stone steps. For that reason, it's recommended to wear shoes with good ankle support. Poles may be useful too if you need extra support coming back down.  

The waterfall is beautiful when...

trailData.name: Appalachian Trail: Woody Gap to Gooch Gap
trailData.description:
Explore the woods of the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest along this point-to-point trail through the woods. It's an easy start from Woody Gap, followed by gently rolling hills and then a gradual descent into Gooch Gap. 

There are two incredible outlooks along the way and a picnic area at Gooch Gap. Most of the trail follows a narrow path with a steep drop to one side. There are lots of big boulders and one rocky section to navigate.

trailData.name: Tranquil Trail
trailData.description:
The Tranquil Trail in High Falls State Park offers a peaceful and scenic hike through lush woodlands. This well-maintained trail features gentle terrain, perfect for a relaxing stroll among tall trees, flowing streams, and vibrant foliage. Ideal for nature lovers and those seeking a quiet retreat in a serene, picturesque setting.

If you have the time, you can add a another short trail from the same parking lot to explore more of the wonderful views of the river and...

trailData.name: West Palisades Chattahoochee River
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: Very well marked. Parking is weird. There is a large lot that is closed and a much smaller lot at the end of the road. If you want an easier hike, walk up to the other lot. Much much easier to get onto trails but further from the river.

trailData.name: Rock Outcrop and Watershed Trail
trailData.description: The hike commences near the Panola Mountain Visitors Center in Panola Mountain State Park. The trail is well-marked and offers breathtaking views, including several lovely overlooks, one of which provides a stunning view of Stone Mountain. Towards the end, the trail features a sustained incline that adds a bit of challenge. Throughout the hike, the air is filled with birdsong, and the trail is lined with wildflowers in spring.

trailData.name: Cauley Creek Park Trail
trailData.description: This is a great trail in a nice urban park. The surface is made of rubber so it's very easy on the knees and feet. About half the course is shady. The other half is exposed to the sun, so it can get pretty hot in the summer. Part of the trail runs along the Chattahoochee River. There are restrooms located at the trail head.

trailData.name: Little Mulberry Trail
trailData.description:
The Little Mulberry Trail winds through stunning natural settings on a combination of paved, dirt, and gravel routes. The trail meanders softly through a meadow frequented by grazing deer on the verdant meadows.

The trail continues into a corridor surrounded by trees. En route, you will come upon a picnic table. The trail then meanders across creek beds, climbs mild slopes, and narrows to a rocky single track.

You'll come to a bench further on. Eventually, the trail ends at a rocky outcrop,...

trailData.name: Henry's Mill Falls Trail to Bear Creek
trailData.description: The Henry's Mill Falls Trail to Bear Creek meanders through a gently rolling forest landscape. Following the trail, you'll cross several streams and navigate a mixed pine and hardwood forest. The trail provides beautiful creek views and leads to an excellent vantage point for observing Henry Mill Falls. The waterfall cascades over a broad, colorful rock outcrop. Be cautious of slippery rocks, particularly near the water.

trailData.name: Bridge Loop Trail and Lake Loop Trail
trailData.description:
This trail is designated for for hiking, birding and pedestrian use only. No mountain biking is allowed. 

As of January 1, 2021, dogs and pets are prohibited from all Chicopee Woods Hiking and Mountain Biking Trails, parking areas, and the Elachee Nature Science Center campus. Please see www.elachee.org for updated rules and trail maps.

There is a $5 daily parking fee or you can purchase a $50 annual pass.

trailData.name: Sibley Pond Loop
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: This marvelous trail explores part of Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area. The journey starts at Scope Creek Parking Area and follows well-marked trails through the woods. The trail has a few roots and stones but is mostly easy to navigate. Visitors can check out the lake and ruins along the way. Throughout the hike, you'll be accompanied by beautiful sounds of water and nature.

trailData.name: Toccoa Swinging Bridge via John Dick Creek Road and Toccoa River Road
trailData.description:
This is a slightly longer approach to the popular Toccoa Swinging Bridge and offers a more quiet and peaceful setting. 

The swinging bridge is located across the Toccoa River, and the majority of visitors access this route on the other side. For a shorter hike to the bridge, see this alternative route https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/georgia/toccoa-swinging-bridge

trailData.name: Pigeon Hill, Brumby Camp, Hardage Mill and Noses Creek Trail
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
This trail begins from Pigeon Hill Trailhead, where parking is available. It explores part of Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park and travels to the summit of Little Kennesaw Mountain. The climb to the top is steep and rocky in places, so it's a good idea to wear shoes with good grip. The remainder of the route follows a gradual downhill gradient. The trails are not marked well, so be sure to have a copy of the map handy. 

Along the way, visitors will be treated to stellar views,...

trailData.name: Big Creek Greenway from Marconi Drive
trailData.description: The trail offers a pleasant, shaded pathway that consists of paved surfaces and boardwalks. It is relatively flat, providing an easy and enjoyable cycling or walking experience. The trailhead is accessed via Marconi Drive. Restrooms are available at Rock Mill Park and the trail's turnaround point. As this is a shared-use trail, please be mindful of others on the path and allow others to pass safely.

trailData.name: Olde Rope Mill Little River Trail
trailData.description: This trail is a fantastic way to explore Olde Rope Mill Park and the banks of Little River. The trailhead is located a short distance from the parking area of Rope Mill Road. From here, the route follows shaded paths that run along both sides of the river. The trestle bridge spanning the river offers fantastic views over the water.

trailData.name: Kennesaw Mountain via Kennesaw Mountain Drive
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This is a straightforward trail with a steady incline to get the heart pumping. Beginning from the Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park Visitor's Center, you'll make your way to the top of Kennesaw Mountain. The skyline views from the top are incredible. The surface is a paved road the whole way, open only to pedestrians on the weekends.

trailData.name: Miller Trek
trailData.description: This trek starts at Brasstown Valley Resort.

trailData.name: Don Carter Hiking Trail Loop
trailData.description: This loop follows the green, yellow, white, and pink blazed trails. This trail is composed of three different hiking trails- it is connector No. 1, and the outer connecting edges of hiking loops 1, 2, and 3.

trailData.name: Two-Mile Backcountry Loop Trail
trailData.description:
Enjoy this wooded trail that provides access to the Cloudland Canyons State Parks back-country campsites.

In a clockwise fashion, the trail slopes gently downward through oak woodland on its way to a small stream and dark groves of eastern hemlock. The trail then climbs approximately 200 feet back to the trailhead.

trailData.name: Allatoona Creek Trail
trailData.description: This trail is popular with mountain bikers but is also open to walkers and runners. It begins from the parking lot off Old Stilesboro Road in Allatoona Creek Park. The route is easy to follow and well-marked. There is plenty of shade throughout the route, with a few exposed sections where you can enjoy some sun.

trailData.name: 24 Gun Trail
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: Located on a small, wooded rise facing Little Kennesaw and Pigeon Hill, this Federal gun emplacement accommodated four batteries, each containing six artillery pieces. These guns bombarded Confederate forces on Kennesaw Mountain off and on for 10 days. Today, four artillery pieces have been placed in the historic earthworks: thee 3 inch ordnance rifles (iron tubes painted black) and one 12 pound Napoleon gun (bronze gun with green oxidation).

trailData.name: Picket Line Trail and Brumby Camp Loop
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: Starting on a gentle incline, the trail continues along an open field before transitioning into the forest. As you progress, the trail widens. The trail eventually leads to a rocky clearing at the summit, offering a great spot to pause and take in the surroundings. Be sure to keep your eyes peeled for the diverse flora and fauna that thrive in this area.

trailData.name: Bear Creek and Pinhoti Loop
trailData.description: This is a nice and quiet hike that winds through a beautiful forest. The trail has plenty of shade and water crossings, which is great for keeping cool in the summer. The backcountry has several campsites, making it a great spot for an overnight stay. The only challenging part is a couple of creek crossings, but most of the time, you can rock hop across. One of the highlights of the trail is the Gennett Poplar, which is the second-largest tree in Georgia.

trailData.name: Sweetwater Creek White, Brown, White and Red
trailData.description: You start by taking the white trail and at the fork fork to the right for the longer distance. Then you go until you get about a mile and change in and you going to take the left at the Brown Trail. When you get to where the brown trail perpendicularly meet the white Trail you go left. you are now on the white trail that will take you next to the creek over several moderate to advanced difficulty rocks as well as some flat surfaces. After two sets of stairs and a few Rocky up he’ll move...

trailData.name: Allatoona Falls Trail via Cherokee County Aquatic Center
trailData.description:
The Allatoona Falls Trail is breathtaking, close to Toonigh Creek's mouth into Lake Allatoona. The falls, also called Toonigh Creek Falls and Allatoona Falls, were formerly known as Hause Shoals. 

This route begins at the Cherokee County Aquatic Center connection to the Allatoona Falls Trail via a short connector trail.
 
The river, waterfall, and rocks can be incredibly slippery, so exercise caution when traversing them. The tranquil atmosphere is further enhanced by the river's mirrored...

trailData.name: Lake Loop Trail
trailData.description:
This trail is designated for for hiking, birding and pedestrian use only. No mountain biking is allowed. 

As of January 1, 2021, dogs and pets are prohibited from all Chicopee Woods Hiking and Mountain Biking Trails, parking areas, and the Elachee Nature Science Center campus. Please see www.elachee.org for updated rules and trail maps.

There is a $5 daily parking fee or you can purchase a $50 annual pass.

trailData.name: Little Ridge Trail
trailData.description:
This is a lovely walk around a sand point of Lake Lanier. The trail is easy to follow, and several connecting trails allow you to adjust the length of the journey and further explore Little Ridge Park. 

This peaceful park is the perfect place to enjoy nature, with great lake views and many small beaches you can easily access from the trail. Most of the trail is through the woods, offering plenty of shade.

trailData.name: Central and Burnt Tree Loop
trailData.description: Although this trail is multi-use, it is particularly popular among mountain bikers in the area.  Hikers should be cautious around blind turns and keep an eye out for bikers. The trail is well-marked and travels through a beautiful forest, offering stunning lake views. There are pit toilets available in the parking area.

trailData.name: Three Forks Loop via Appalachian and Benton Mackaye Trail
trailData.description: Begin this beautiful hike at the Three Forks Trailhead. You will start by wandering through a scenic and lush forest on the Appalachian Trail. The trail parallels Stover Creek and provides excellent resting areas along the water and great water fill-up sources. There are several great camping options along this portion of the trail. Halfway through, the trail connects with the Benton MacKaye Trail and begins the return to the trailhead.

trailData.name: Montgomery Falls and Lower Black Falls
trailData.description:
Plan ahead and Prepare—this route is not a Forest Service system trail and is not maintained for public access. Visitors should be aware that they are likely to encounter adverse conditions and do so at their own risk.

This is a beautiful and scenic creek hike! The route begins at a small trailhead located on Camp Merrill Access Road, with enough space to accommodate about three cars. The trail is well-maintained, but please note that there is no signage along the path. It is advisable to...

trailData.name: Cochran Shoals West Loop from Interstate North Trailhead
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description:
Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area is a lovely place for a walk, run, or bike ride. This route explores a series of trails in the western region of the park. The terrain is paved and flat at the beginning and the end of this route. 

The middle section of the trail is mostly dirt, mud, and clay and features a little more elevation gain. These areas can get slippery after rain, so it's a good idea to wear shoes with good traction.

trailData.name: Heritage Park Trail
trailData.description:
Starting from the parking lot off Nickajack Road this route heads into the forest and travels alongside Nickajack Creek. Sections of the route follow an elevated boardwalk over that passes over wetlands. The trail's turn around point is at the historic Concord Covered Bridge and Ruff's Mill. 

The park's main entrance is at the intersection of Fontaine and Nickajack Roads. Here, there is ample parking, restrooms, and picnic spots.

trailData.name: Creek Trail, Sequoyah's Return and Cherokee Loop
trailData.description: The trail is easy with the length easily adjusted for any hiker's abilities.The trail is well marked with a map at kios' a major trail intersections. The trail is also very will maintained. Turner Reservoir is a nice feature along with a nice, but  a small set of rapids on Turner Creek which feeds the reservoir. You do have to walk a short distance off the established trail to view these rapids. There were some wildflowers and a number of blooming trees along the way, although not as showy as...

trailData.name: Big Rock, Gahuti, Goldmine Creek, Lake
trailData.description: This is a spectacular trail in Fort Mountain State Park. The route travels through the woods and features some stunning views early on. The route is well-shaded but can get very narrow in some parts. There is lots of elevation change throughout the journey, as well as roots and rocks to navigate. Keep an eye out for wildlife, including black bears, turkeys, and squirrels.  Bring bug spray for mosquitoes if you're visiting in spring or summer.

trailData.name: Allatoona Lake via Cooper's Furnace Trail
trailData.description:
This trail closes seasonally, for up to date information, see the park page here: https://www.sam.usace.army.mil/Missions/Civil-Works/Recreation/Allatoona-Lake/Day-Use/Cooper-Furnace-park/

Users have suggested that the trail is a little more fun (technical) once you switch to the Laurel Ridge Trail which has frequent red blazes. Cooper Furnace Trail has bluish-green blazes. It is only 0.2 miles or so extra to see the overlook above the Visitor's Center.

trailData.name: Harbins Park Trail
trailData.description: The trail is open for hiking and biking, but it is particularly popular among mountain bikers in the area. The surface is mostly natural singletrack with some sections of pavement. The trail consists of three main loops, including one large loop and two smaller ones. It's a very twisty trail, with lots of roots, and there are few hills to climb and descend. Overall, this trail is a fantastic part of the Gwinnett County park system.

trailData.name: The Ridge Nature Area Loop
trailData.description:
Nestled between Gingercake Creek and Whitewater Creek, the Ridge includes 308 acres of natural beauty which provide a glimpse into a multitude of ecosystems, opportunities for environmental education and a diverse mix of passive recreational experiences.

The Ridge is a City of Fayetteville public greenspace project. After years of desiring to develop the nature area, the City engaged Southern Conservation Trust to develop and manage the public use nature area. A Master Vision Plan has been...

trailData.name: Johns Mountain and Pinhoti Loop
trailData.description: The trail can be accessed from either the Keown Falls parking lot or the John's Mountain parking lot. The falls are impressive during wet seasons and the trail passes through a large space behind the falls.

trailData.name: Middle Oconee Structure Number One Dam
Settles Bridge Loop
trailData.description: The Settles Bridge Loop provides a scenic hike with beautiful views of the Chattahoochee River. The trail meanders through meadows and woodland areas. As you hike, you'll encounter mild inclines and footbridges that help you cross various small streams. The trail closely follows the river, allowing for picturesque views. Wildlife sightings, such as deer, add to the trail's appeal.

trailData.name: Dauset Nature Center Loop [CLOSED]
trailData.description:
The Dauset Trails Nature Center offers an extensive network of interconnecting trails for biking and hiking alike. This trail can very easily be made into a shorter or longer journey.

Dogs are allowed on hike and bike trails with a 6-foot leash. Dogs are not allowed inside the fenced-in nature center area.

trailData.name: Miller Lake and East Mulberry Equestrian Loop
trailData.description:
This trail winds through shaded forests and meadows and follows the shores of Lake Miller at Little Mulberry Park. It is a popular destination for horseback riding and hiking, and benches and picnic tables are available for rest breaks along the way.

Expect some steep, rocky sections with roots and stones, so sturdy footwear is recommended. A parking lot with restrooms is located at the trailhead.

trailData.name: Dwelling Loop (Intermediate)
trailData.description: Su/Mon/Wed/Fri are clockwise. Tue/Thurs/Sat are counter-clockwise.

trailData.name: Sawnee Mountain West: Extended Loop
trailData.description: Approach trails of the Sawnee Mountain Preserve's Mountainside Trail.

trailData.name: Amicalola Creek Trail
trailData.location_label: Dawson Forest Wildlife Management Area, Georgia
trailData.description:
Each person (age 16+) MUST possess a valid hunting license, fishing license, or Georgia Lands Pass to enter this property (EVEN IF YOU ARE NOT HUNTING OR FISHING!). This can be purchased online at gooutdoorsgeorgia.com or by calling 1-800-366-2661. All persons must have proof of purchase for their Hunting License, Fishing License, or Georgia Lands Pass on their person while on the property. This is strictly enforced.

According to wheelchairtraveling.com: The Amicalola River Trail in...

trailData.name: Sope Creek Short Loop
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: This is a peaceful trail in Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area. It starts from the Sope Creek Parking Area and winds its way towards Sibley Pond. The path meanders through beautiful forest and passes near Sope Creek Paper Mills Creek (an option detour). There are many intersecting paths along this route. Having a copy of the map with you is best to ensure you follow the right path. There are lots of roots and rocks on the trail.

trailData.name: East and West Trail Loop
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: The East and West Trail Loop begins as a wide dirt and gravel path but becomes increasingly rocky as it ascends. This uphill climb can be steep in sections. As you make your way up the trail, you’ll have the chance to spot wildlife such as deer in their natural habitat. The hike leads to an overlook platform at the top of Kennesaw Mountain. From this vantage point, you can enjoy stunning panoramic views of downtown Atlanta, the Buckhead skyline, and Stone Mountain.

trailData.name: Murphey Candler Park Trail
trailData.description:
Beautiful well established trail through the woods around the lake.

This trail is very well established and easy to traverse.  There are a few small sections that include rocks and roots, but typically it is hard packed dirt or sidewalk.  Any streams, water or troublesome areas are easily traversed by way of sturdily built bridges.

1.6 mile trail loop.  2 loops is 5K (3.1 Mi) and 4 loops is 10k (6.2 mi)

trailData.name: Line Creek Nature Area
trailData.description: This is a lovely hike in Line Creek Nature Area. It features lovely wooded trails and peaceful creeks. Starting from the parking lot of Line Creek Drive, the path winds through the forest and passes by Flying Biscuit Pond. The trail is well-shaded, and there are picnic benches along it where you can stop and take a break. There are also bathrooms at the trailhead.

trailData.name: Chattahoochee River Loop
trailData.description: The trail is reportedly not well marked so you may want to download the offline map before you go.

trailData.name: King's Trail at Indian Island
trailData.description: King's Trail at Indian Island winds through a wooded area filled with towering trees and a lush forest canopy. You may catch glimpses of the shimmering Stone Mountain Lake as you hike. The trail winds along the shoreline, providing access to benches, picnic areas, and rocky outcroppings. Along the way, you'll encounter a variety of flora and fauna.

trailData.name: East Benton MacKaye Trail to Fall Branch Falls and Stanley Gap Trail
trailData.description: This trail takes you through a breathtaking, dense forest to the magnificent Fall Branch Falls. The hike begins at the Benton MacKaye Trailhead, where you'll be immediately immersed in the beauty of the North Georgia wilderness. The trail is well-maintained and is especially stunning during the fall season when the leaves are changing colors. Fall Branch Falls is a 30-foot waterfall that cascades over a long rock slab. It's a great spot to take a break before continuing on to Stanley Gap,...

trailData.name: Sweet Gum, Homestead and Iron Hill Trail
trailData.location_label: Red Top Mountain State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This route takes you along a well-marked trail on a relatively flat surface through the Red Top Mountain State Park area. This area is best known for the 12,000-acre Lake Allatoona that borders the park. You can do many water activities on the lake, including swimming, water skiing, and fishing. There are also more than 15 miles of trails to explore.

trailData.name: Simpsonwood Loop Trail
trailData.description:
Simpsonwood is named after its donor, Ludie Simpson, who bequeathed 223 pristine acres with frontage on the Chattahoochee River to the Methodist church in 1973 with the understanding that it would not be subdivided or developed. The church operated a lodge/conference center on the property, but at a loss and decided to sell. Fortunately, Gwinnett County was able to procure the property in 2016. 

The goal is for the park to lean more toward a nature preserve than a community park with minimal...

trailData.name: Powers Island Loop Trail
trailData.description: Powers Island is also a great spot to hop in a kayak and spend some time exploring the river.

trailData.name: Tribble Mill Park Loop
trailData.description:
Tribble Hill Park is home to a dense network of trails, and this route is largely a perimeter route made up of many segments.
 It is definitely a choose-your-own-adventure trail system! It's advised to download the map so you don't get turned around. 

This is a great trail for dog walkers, trail runners and hikers.

trailData.name: Tsalaki Trail and Wetlands Loop
trailData.description: The trail meanders through a lush hardwood forest, following the gentle course of a creek. As you continue, you'll encounter a picnic table. The trail features several footbridges crossing over small streams. Eventually, you'll arrive at the heart of a sunflower field. Further along, the trail takes you to an old covered bridge spanning Dukes Creek.

trailData.name: Jarrard Gap, Slaughter Creek, and Appalachian Trail Loop
trailData.description: This is a gorgeous trail that winds through a lush forest and combines multiple trails. Unlike most approach trails, it does not get particularly steep near the AT. The trail offers a lovely loop trip by going up the Jarrard Gap Trail, up to Bird Gap on the AT, and then back down the Slaughter Creek Trail to its shared trailhead with the Jarrard Gap Trail.

trailData.name: Gahuti Inner Loop to West Overlook, Fort Mountain, and Cool Springs
trailData.description: This loop trail is a nice hike through the woods. You’ll hike to a couple of scenic overlooks, a cool fire tower, water features, and the mysterious rock wall. Near the top, there is a fire tower, Fort Mountain Rock Fort, which offers an incredible overlook. The trail is narrow in some parts and has many roots and rocks. There are restrooms available in the parking lot.

trailData.name: White Tail Trail
trailData.location_label: Red Top Mountain State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: The Whitetail Trail meanders along the edge of Lake Allatoona, leading to a stunning overlook. Large rocks along the way offer excellent vantage points of Lake Allatoona and are also ideal spots for fishing or simply relaxing by the water. Keep your eyes peeled for the flora and fauna that inhabit this area.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Snodgrass Hill Loop
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
This trail starts from Lafayette Road and explores part of Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park. The trail is not very well marked, and it's easy to get off the path due to the numerous options for mini trails and service roads. 

Along the trail, you'll encounter historic markers, signs, platforms, and memorial statues. The trail surface varies between asphalt, gravel, loose dirt, and rocks. Wildlife sightings may include deer, butterflies, owls, and other bird species.

trailData.name: Lake Chatuge Loop
trailData.description: Beautiful lake side trail with scenic views suitable for nature enthusiasts of all levels. It’s good running it for a high intensity workout and for those easy afternoon/morning strolls.

trailData.name: Bluff, Turkey, Jedi and Middle Trail Loop
trailData.description:
The Lula Lake Land Trust is on private property and is open for hiking on very limited days. Please do not try to hike here during closed times. There are a number of limited passes available through lulalake.org before arrival. The core preserve is only open on the first and last weekends of each month to hiking and biking. 

May-November
First and Last Weekends
9:00 a.m.- 5:00 p.m. Saturdays and 12 p.m.-5:00 p.m. Sundays. 

November-April 
Open the first and last Saturdays only. 

There are...

trailData.name: Pickett's Mill Red and White Loop
trailData.description: The Pickett's Mill Red and White Loop offers a stunning view of the ravine from an overlook. The trail is covered with pine cones, but be cautious of roots along the way. Upon reaching the creek, you'll cross a wooden bridge. The trail narrows as you ascend from the creek area. Along the way, there are several benches where you can take in the peaceful surroundings. Following the trail along the creek, you'll eventually arrive at the site of the historic mill.

trailData.name: Morningside Nature Trail
trailData.description:
This trail winds through dense, jungle-like vegetation, with diverse and varying landscapes to enjoy. With some changes in elevation, this trail is somewhat brief but can provide a decent challenge. 

The major payoff is a spot on the river underneath the suspension bridge, affectionately called "Dog Beach" by locals, where hikers allow their dogs to play in the water while off-leash.

trailData.name: Bearden Falls
trailData.description:
Plan ahead and Prepare—this route is not a Forest Service system trail and is not maintained for public access. Visitors should be aware that they are likely to encounter adverse conditions and do so at their own risk.


The trailhead is just to the left as you pull into the parking area. You will cross a creek and travel on a road that is used by off-road vehicles for a bit, and then it becomes foot traffic only. You will cross several small water areas.

To reach the top of the falls for...

trailData.name: Lake Peachtree Loop
trailData.description: This loop trail starts at the parking lot off Willowbend Road, where restrooms and a playground are available, and circles around Lake Peachtree. The path winds through local parks, forested areas, and residential neighborhoods, passing Spyglass Island and following the shoreline with lovely water views. Keep an eye out for deer, ducks, turkeys, geese, and other wildlife along the way.

trailData.name: Whitley Gap Shelter Trail
trailData.description:
A hiking trail in the North Georgia Mountains. The beginning portion is along the Appalachian Trail.

This trail begins with a small section of the Appalachian Trail that ascends Wildcat Mountain from Hogpen Gap. From there the trail forks to the left from the AT and descends down Wildcat Mountain. There are great views from the top of Wildcat Mountain as well as a couple of campsites.

trailData.name: Chattahoochee Bend Riverside-Bend Trail
trailData.description:
The Riverside-Bend Trail at Chattahoochee Bend State Park is a volunteer-built-and-maintained 5 mile (10 miles out and back) trail located near Newnan, Georgia, that features riverviews and is rated easy-to-moderate. Dogs are welcome but must be kept on leash.

The first two miles are on the riverbank and feature creek crossings and a 30' tower at 0.8 mile. It intersects the Tower Trail at 0.9 mile. Two miles up the trail turns away from the river and meanders through hardwood...

trailData.name: Ravine Loop Trail
trailData.description: Explore Little Mulberry Park via this exceptional trail. The walk begins from the parking lot on Little Mulberry-Fence Road. The path is a mix of cement and gravel and winds through gorgeous hardwood forests. A few slight inclines along the way will get the blood pumping. There are bathrooms at the start of the trail.

trailData.name: Ropers Rock and Bluff Trail from Point Park
trailData.description: Discover the breathtaking views of the Tennessee River and Chattanooga from the summit of Lookout Mountain. This route will take you through Point Park and into the forest, where you will witness stunning sandstone cliffs, enchanting caves, and charming small waterfalls. Along the way, you will also come across a few historical markers that provide insights into the region's war and land history.

trailData.name: Reynolds Nature Preserve Trail
trailData.description: This route takes you around the Reynolds Nature Preserve along Cypress Spring on a quick hike along a well-maintained trail with enjoyable elevation changes. You will pass by some fantastic ponds with a nice dock to enjoy panoramic views of the waters. The route connects to several other trails if you would like to extend your hike and explore the surrounding area.

trailData.name: Yellow River Park Loop
trailData.description: Yellow River Park is a multi-user trail system, with no directionality (users may go either directions on their specific trail. Bicycles yield to hikers and both bicycles and hikers yield to equestrians.

trailData.name: Paper Mill Ruins
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: This route travels through thick hardwood forest downhill to 2 paper mill ruins. The ruins at SC27 lie on the west bank of Sope Creek while the SC29 ruins are on the other side of the creek and a bit further south where the small Caney Creek tributary pours into the larger creek. The structures were destroyed by the Union army during the Civil War and remnants still stand tall against the beautiful backdrop of tall trees and steady flowing water.

trailData.name: Appalachian Trail: Cooper Gap to Woody Gap
trailData.description: Medium difficulty, not as strenuous and technical as trail sections around Springer Mountain. Car park at Woody gap gets full early on weekends

trailData.name: Buzzard's Roost Loop
trailData.description:
Discover the beauty of Rocky Face Ridge Park via this adventurous trail.
The trail features numerous switchbacks and offers breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape. It is quite rocky and requires navigating through challenging terrain. Hikers should be cautious of Timber Rattler snakes along the trail. Access to the trailhead is available via Crow Valley Road, where parking is available.

trailData.name: Short Loop via Gold Branch Trail
trailData.description: There is a parking fee of $5 at this trailhead.

trailData.name: Chandler Lake Loop
trailData.description: This is a lovely trail in Tribble Mill Park. The area offers a stunning view of the lake, where people can often be seen fishing. The trail consists of paved sections and natural terrain with roots and rocks. The picturesque scenery around the lake, complete with benches strategically placed along the way, provides ample opportunities to rest and enjoy the beauty. Wildlife like geese, cranes, and turtles can often be spotted here.

trailData.name: Rocky Mountain via Stanley Gap
trailData.description: This trail starts at the parking lot off Aska Road and leads to Rocky Mountain via Stanley Gap. It ascends through the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest, reaching the summit with beautiful long-range views. The best views are during the winter months when the trees are dormant. Be prepared for rocky sections—sturdy footwear is recommended.

trailData.name: Raccoon Mountain Reservoir Loop
trailData.description:
The Raccoon Mountain Trail System, high above Chattanooga, Tennessee, offers trail runners the perfect terrain for distance running. The views from along the trail are simply stunning so make sure to stop and take a breather or two and take in the spectacular scenery. 

With a variety of trail options and unmatched views of the surrounding mountains, this trail is an example of what can happen when you allow recreational access to public land. It is clean, well used, and represents the nature...

trailData.name: Cochran Mill Yellow Trail
trailData.description: Single track trail shared between hikers and bikers. Signs at the trailhead indicate that bikes should yield to hikers. Please share the trail respectfully.

trailData.name: Fort Yargo West Dam via Inner Trail
trailData.description: The trail starts by crossing a bridge that connects to the Inner Loop trail. It runs alongside the Marbury Creek Watershed, offering stunning views of the water. The route concludes at the dam, but there are possibilities to extend the path for those who wish to do so. This is a multi-use trail that can be used by both hikers and bikers.

trailData.name: Ivy Creek Greenway to Wildlife Observation Trail
trailData.description: Apart from the actual environmental center, there are various interlocking trails from .5 to 1.5 miles long. They range from easy to moderate to difficult and make for a very fun experience that you can make as short or as long as you want.

trailData.name: Council of Trees Trail
trailData.description: This route takes you on a short hike along a well-maintained trail on the Council of Trees Trail. The trail is mostly packed gravel with some rooty sections. It provides a nice variety of uphill and downhill terrain but is not too strenuous. The trail gets narrow in some areas, and Poison Ivy is present as well, so make sure you come prepared.

trailData.name: Sweetwater Creek Blue Loop via Yellow and Orange Trails
trailData.description: This rout starts on the yellow trail and makes its way to blue and orange. It features moderate inclines and narrow trails on the blue loop. Wander through the beautiful forest and check out the Ferguson Mill Ruins.

trailData.name: Fort Mountain Lake Loop
trailData.description:
This is a terrific scenic trail in Fort Mountain State Park. The route follows a well-maintained path with clear markers. The trail is mostly shaded, creating a peaceful ambiance with the delightful accompaniment of birdsong. Along the way, an incredible scenic overlook provides a beautiful view of the lake.

The path around the lake consists mainly of gravel, transitioning to a smooth but occasionally rutted and rocky trail. Benches are strategically placed along the way where you can take...

trailData.name: Pinhoti South Trail
trailData.location_label: James H. (Sloppy) Floyd State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This trail starts at the parking lot off Sloppy Floyd Lake Road and leads into James H. (Sloppy) Floyd State Park. You’ll come across a marble mine cave with a small waterfall trickle and wooden boardwalk. Be prepared for exposed tree roots and steep, rocky sections in the forest—sturdy footwear is recommended.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Upper Truck Trail to Bluff Trail Loop
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Tennessee
trailData.description: This trail starts at the parking lot near Cravens House and leads into the Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park. Cravens House, built in 1856 by ironmaster Robert Cravens, is one of the oldest remaining structures on Lookout Mountain. You'll find a mix of rocky terrain, stairs, and a few technical sections near Sunset Rock as you hike. Your efforts will be rewarded with breathtaking views of Chattanooga and the winding Tennessee River below.

trailData.name: Fort Yargo Outer Mountain Bike Trail
trailData.description: The trail system is excellent—well-marked and easy to navigate. It offers both beginner and advanced routes, allowing you to choose the level of challenge that suits you. It's a great area to enjoy nature and have fun outdoors. If you're interested in getting a yearly pass, be sure to check with the park staff in the front building; they are very friendly and helpful.

trailData.name: Benton MacKaye Duncan Ridge Trail: Morganton Highway to Toccoa River
trailData.description: The Benton MacKaye Duncan Ridge Trail features a highlight of an impressive suspension bridge that spans the river. The trail includes a steady ascent and traverses a series of small knobs along a long ridgeline. Hikers are rewarded with stunning scenery and panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. Along the way, you’ll encounter diverse flora and fauna.

trailData.name: Gooch Gap to Cooper Gap via Appalachian Trail
trailData.description: It is a great section of the Appalachian Trail from Gooch Gap to Cooper Gap. The trail is in the woods along Justus Creek. It has some elevation gains with gradual climbs and a few creek crossings. It is well-maintained, making it a great place to enjoy nature and a relaxing hike. Along the way, there are a variety of camping sites.

trailData.name: Lake Trahlyta Waterfall
trailData.description: This trail can be accessed from the end of Vogel State Park, where the trailhead offers a parking lot, restrooms, a pavilion, a beach, a shelter, and the John B. Derden CCC Museum. It’s a short hike along the shores of Lake Trahlyta, leading to a small waterfall with an observation deck overlooking Wolf Creek.

trailData.name: George W. Disney Trail
trailData.description: This trail starts out easy but quickly ascends. Once at the top, there is an old Civil War general grave site.

trailData.name: Suwanee Creek Greenway
trailData.description: The Suwanee Creek Greenway winds through wetlands and scenic hardwood forests, home to a vibrant array of frogs, turtles, and waterfowl. The marshes border the trail and flow beneath its boardwalks. You may spot deer through the wooded landscape. Keep your eyes peeled for plants along the way.

trailData.name: Clinton Nature Preserve Loop
trailData.description: Located just outside of Atlanta in Villa Rica, GA, is the Clinton Nature Reserve sitting at 200-acres. The park has nature trails and other open areas for exploration, including the Carnes Cabin, which is a pre-Civil War residence listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The park is open seven days a week from dawn to dusk.

trailData.name: GEHC Stream Ecology Trail
trailData.description: This loop trail, part of the Gwinnett Environmental Heritage Center, offers several terrific up-and-down paths as it winds through the forest. In wet conditions, sections of the trail can become quite muddy and may even be impassable. The trail begins near the Treetop Quest, a ropes course combined with zip lines.

trailData.name: Mountainside Trail Loop via Tower Road
trailData.description: Sawnee Mountain Preserve has five main trails to explore and this loop combines Mountainside Trail and Church Trail. It is a pleasant wooded trail with good elevation change. It is a good workout route with some inlcine and rocky in places. You can park at the church parking lot and it has limited space.

trailData.name: Rock Springs Park Loop
trailData.description:
The Rock Springs Park Trail is a combination of hard and soft surfaces.  This trail traverses a creek system that divides the park into narrow ravines, hilltops, and ridges.

The combination of multi-use asphalt and mulched nature trail meanders through mature woodland and an open area, crosses creeks using a boardwalk, two footbridges, and a suspension bridge, and edges around a lily pond.

Nearby you can also find a football field, three soccer fields, tennis courts, a dog park, a small...

trailData.name: Bethesda Park Trail
trailData.description: Bethesda Park Trail winds around a pond, surrounded by beautiful, wooded areas that provide ample shade. As you walk, the serene environment offers frequent sightings of local wildlife, including deer. The trail includes a few gentle inclines. Some parts of the trail may be muddy and slippery, especially after rainfall, so caution is advised.

trailData.name: Rickimberly Sanftner Trail
trailData.description: This trail follows the perimeter of Haig Mill Lake Park and offers a relaxing trail with calm lake views. It is on a wide path through the woods. There are several fishing piers and benches along the trail.  Swimming and wading in the lake are prohibited and for fishing, you have to have a valid Georgia Fishing License. The trailhead has a kayak dock, a playground, restrooms, and a pavilion.

trailData.name: Blueway Trail
trailData.description:
This trail is short and well maintained by the nature preserve. It loops around the creek using two bridges and is very good for small children.

Blue Heron Nature Preserve is a 501(c)3 nonprofit dedicated to protecting 30 acres in North Buckhead; home of the 3-mile Blueway Trail.

Blue Heron offers hands-on education programming for children and adults of all ages: bhnp.org

trailData.name: Bowmans Island and Laurel Ridge Trails
trailData.description: The Bowmans Island and Laurel Ridge Trails meanders through forested hills and along the riverbanks. Deer are often sighted along the trail. A highlight of the trail is a viewing platform that provides an excellent view of Bowman’s Island Unit. At one point of the trail, you’ll cross a wooden bridge and use a boulder for an easy crossing. You can find a bench near the wooden bridge. The trail also passes through a set of impressive stone pillars.

trailData.name: Sope Creek via Powers Ferry Trail
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description:
Enjoy this beautiful trail that starts off following Sope Creek before heading into the park and exploring the lush forest. There are many great sights along this trail, including some ruins. 
The trail is well-maintained and mostly well-marked, but the many intersecting trails can make it a little tricky, so download the map to be safe.

trailData.name: Leone Hall Price Creek Loop
trailData.description: This is the outer perimeter loop at Leone Hall Price Park that takes visitors to the creek. This well-maintained loop trail meanders alongside Price Creek, winding through lush woodlands and serene meadows. The trail features gentle terrain, making it accessible for hikers of all skill levels, including families and casual walkers.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Mountain Beautiful Trail to Ropers Rock
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Tennessee
trailData.description: As you climb gradually toward the summit, the Mountain Beautiful Trail rewards hikers with beautiful views of Lookout Mountain and the surrounding Tennessee Valley. The trail takes you to Ropers Rock, a scenic outcrop that provides breathtaking panoramic views of the battlefield below and the surrounding landscape, with distant hills and valleys stretching as far as the eye can see.

trailData.name: Cherokee Falls to Hemlock Falls via Bear Creek Trail
trailData.description: Cloudland Canyon State Park offers an excellent opportunity for exploration with its waterfalls, pools, rapids, and scenic vistas. The terrain along this trail is rocky and rugged, with some areas that can be slippery. There are numerous stairs to navigate to reach the waterfalls, so visitors should be prepared for that. Arrive early to avoid the crowds. Parking is available at the start of the trail.

trailData.name: Johnson Ferry Extended Loop
trailData.description:
This is a walking trail along the Chattahoochee River. Please note that there are two different trails with different parking areas and starting points. Johnson Ferry South and North. This is the North loop.

An easy walking trail that follows the Chattahoochee River. A return loop can be made by following a parallel trail along the buried oil pipeline. There is also an extension trail that leads up a creek to the north with some interesting small cliffs and rocky stream.

trailData.name: Laurel Falls Trail Loop
trailData.description: This route takes you on the orange-blazed trail along Laurel Falls Trail, passing Laurel and Lost Falls. The best times to visit the falls are late fall, spring, and winter. The falls are normally dry in the summer unless you come after rainfall. The trails are well-marked but can get narrow and overgrown in some areas.

trailData.name: Chastain Park Trail
trailData.description:
A 3-mile loop around Atlanta's largest park. Very family-friendly park and trail. Some hills, but it’s very stroller friendly and dog friendly.

Accessibility: There are 6 designated accessible spaces in the large paved parking lot off of West Wieuca Road Northwest at the north end of the trail. All of them are van-accessible with striped access aisles. The trail surface is paved asphalt or concrete (with railings at bridges). It is typically 4 to 6 feet wide (with some wider passing spaces)....

trailData.name: Upper Guild Trail
trailData.description:
This is the upper section of the Guild Trail at the Ruby Falls entrance. To access the trailhead, drive into the main Ruby Falls attraction entrance (at the big sign) and drive to the back of the parking lot- there will be a small gated gravel parking lot on your left at the turn. 

This is a wide, gravel stroll in the woods. Gravel riders and trail runners use this trail and there are many options to connect to different trails.

trailData.name: Big Creek Walking Loop
trailData.description: This route starts at the Roswell Greenway Parking area and takes you along a nice, well-maintained path in the Big Creek Greenway area. This trail takes you through a lush green area with some nice bridge crossings, adding to its charm. This area also includes hiking and biking trails, making it a great place for anyone.

trailData.name: Etowah River Park Loop
trailData.description: This is a marvelous route that travels alongside the Etowah River. The path offers stunning views and some shaded areas. It is partially paved, mostly flat, and wide enough for bikers, walkers, and dogs to use the trail. Parking is available at the start of the trail near the playground in  Heritage Park.

trailData.name: Trail of the Muscogee
trailData.description:
Short, relatively easy, trail just past the Stone Mountain Park entrance featuring some nice lakeside views and easy hiking.

The first half of the path follows along the lakeside and then makes a gradual ascent until reaching the ridge adjacent to Highway 78.  From here, it descends back down until reaching the trailhead for a total of 1.5 miles.  Parking is limited to a small lot, but the trail is not usually busy, though well-traveled.

trailData.name: Jackrabbit Mountain Trail
trailData.description: Traveling counter-clockwise, the trail gradually ascends to the summit of Jackrabbit Mountain, providing stunning views along the way. After reaching the top, the path descends back to the lakeside, making this route a fantastic choice for those seeking a mix of woodland walking and picturesque lakeside scenery. Enjoy the best of both worlds!

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Snodgrass House
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Georgia

trailData.name: Wildcat Creek and Turner Trail
trailData.location_label: Dawson Forest Wildlife Management Area, Georgia
trailData.description: All individuals aged 16 and above are required to have a valid hunting license, fishing license, or Georgia Lands Pass to access this property, even if they are not hunting or fishing. These permits can be obtained online at gooutdoorsgeorgia.com or by calling 1-800-366-2661. It is mandatory for all individuals to carry proof of their Hunting License, Fishing License, or Georgia Lands Pass while on the property. Enforcement of this requirement is strict.

trailData.name: Big Rock Nature Trail
trailData.description:
Though Big Rock Nature Trail is a short trail in distance, the rocky scramble involved earns this route a "moderate" rating, as sections of the hike would be challenging for beginning hikers or anyone unaccustomed to scrambling over rocky and uneven surfaces. 

Enjoy a stunning waterfall and lush green forest on this trail outing.

trailData.name: Wilburn Farm and Cascade Trails Loop
trailData.description: A well-maintained trail route through Arabia Mountain Park. Quiet trails for walking and hiking. Lots of wildlife as well.

trailData.name: Sweetwater Creek: Jack's Lake and Bronner Road Loop
trailData.description: Sweetwater Creek Park has color-coded nature trails with various difficulties for all levels. The trail consists of boardwalks, stairs, and regular trails. Some parts of the trail follow right next to Sweetwater Creek, so it can be muddy when the water is high. Along this loop, you can see New Manchester Mill Ruins and a small waterfall. At the trailhead is the Sweetwater Creek Park Visitor Center, which has an educational exhibition about the area's history and ecosystems.

trailData.name: Walden Creek Waterfall Trail
trailData.description:
Plan ahead and Prepare—this route is not a Forest Service system trail and is not maintained for public access. Visitors should be aware that they are likely to encounter adverse conditions and do so at their own risk.

This is a short trail that leads to the beautiful Walden Creek Waterfall. The terrain includes a mix of dirt paths, roots, and occasional rocky sections, requiring sturdy footwear and careful footing. As the trail ascends slightly, hikers will encounter a few small stream...

trailData.name: Turtle Back Loop (Pitner Rd Dog Park Trails)
trailData.description: This route departs from the Pitner Rd Dog Park area and follows the Turtle Back Loop, which features some nice hills along a well-maintained trail. The terrain is a nice mix of dirt and a boardwalk in a lush forest that stays mostly shaded along the way. Navigation in this area can be challenging, so downloading the route beforehand is recommended.

trailData.name: Allatoona Pass Battlefield Trail
trailData.description: The Allatoona Pass Battlefield Trail offers a scenic and historic walk through a significant Civil War site in northern Georgia. This easy trail takes you through the Allatoona Pass Battlefield, where Union and Confederate forces clashed during the Civil War. Along the way, you'll pass interpretive signs, monuments and earthworks that provide insight into the battle and the area's history. The trail winds through peaceful woodlands, offering a quiet, reflective atmosphere with a mix of...

trailData.name: Lanier Point Trail
trailData.description: The Lanier Point Trail in Georgia offers a beautiful and peaceful outdoor experience along the shores of Lake Lanier. This straight forward trail winds through scenic forest areas, offering excellent views of the lake and surrounding area. The trail is great for hikers looking to enjoy a tranquil atmosphere, with plenty of opportunities for birdwatching, photography, and simply soaking in the beauty of the water and woods.

trailData.name: Terrace & Spring Trail Loop
trailData.description: The Terrace Spring Trail Loop offers a quiet, wooded hike through Georgia's lush landscapes in Cascade Springs Nature Preserve. The trail takes you along creeks and through dense forest, with occasional views of springs and wetland areas. It’s a relatively short loop, providing a peaceful escape into nature with a mix of shaded paths and open areas to explore.

trailData.name: DeSoto Falls Bluff View Trail
