trailData.description: DeSoto Falls Bluff View Trail is a quick and mellow trail with a great payoff. This trail leads to an overlook through the woods, not the basin. There are a few drop-offs close to the trail edge, and rocks on the trail can be slippery, so watch your footing. There is a small parking lot at the trailhead.

trailData.area_name: Little Cedar Mountain Small Wild Area
trailData.name: Little Cedar Mountain Trail
trailData.location_label: Little Cedar Mountain Small Wild Area, Tennessee
trailData.description: Both Little Cedar and Cedar Mountain hug the western shoreline of the Tennessee River/Nickajack Lake as the tail-end of Walden Ridge is broken up in the Tennessee River gorge and blends into the Sequatchie valley. The elevation gain and topography grant the Little Cedar Mountain Trail a dry side and a moist side; the wildlife and plants present reflect these subtle changes thus making the two loop trails a somewhat different experience as you hike within the parcel. The trail is owned and...

trailData.name: Trace, Yellow and Purple Trail Loop
trailData.description: The Trace Trail, the white-blazed portion of the trail, starts at the Boling Park Trailhead, at the rear of Boling Park.  At 0.66 miles the Trace trail crosses the Frank Stone memorial bridge.  Immediately after crossing the bridge the Yellow trail (trailhead post with Yellow blaze) begins.  The Yellow trail, a point-to-point trail, makes a one mile, slow uphill climb to its intersection with the Purple trail.  Along the way the Yellow trail follows a couple of beautiful meandering streams,...

trailData.name: Dicks Creek Gap to Powell Mountain
trailData.description: The hike from Dicks Creek Gap to Powell Mountain offers breathtaking views, including vistas of Lake Burton and the surrounding mountains. Along the trail, you’ll also catch sight of notable landmarks like Black Rock Mountain and Rabun Bald. There are some steep sections. Be cautious on parts of the trail with loose rocks. You’ll also navigate a creek crossing.

trailData.name: Cool Springs Overlook
trailData.description: This is a very short walk for a big payoff with great views. One of the highlights of this trail is the overlook at the top, which offers panoramic views of the surrounding mountains, valleys, and forests. On clear days, visitors can enjoy breathtaking vistas of the Cohutta Wilderness and other nearby peaks, providing an excellent spot for taking in the expansive beauty of the region. The overlook also provides a serene spot for picnicking.

trailData.name: Never Never Land Loop
trailData.description: This trail starts at Lost Falls Trailhead, a popular mountain biking loop in DeSoto State Park. It goes along a mix of dirt and rocky terrain with some boardwalks, and there are some enjoyable hills. On the southern end of the loop, there is also a backcountry camping site. The trail can be difficult to navigate, so it's recommended that you download the route before you go.

trailData.name: Environmental Trail Loop
trailData.location_label: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park, Georgia
trailData.description: The Environmental Trail Loop in Georgia is a short and scenic loop trail, ideal for those looking for an easy hike. The trail winds through a peaceful environment, offering views of local flora and fauna. The loop is typically well-maintained and accessible, making it perfect for families, beginners, or anyone looking to enjoy a relaxing walk. The trail also provides educational signage, offering insights into the area's natural environment.

trailData.area_name: Rich Mountain Wildlife Management Area: Cartecay River Tract
trailData.name: Cartecay River North Loop Trail
trailData.location_label: Rich Mountain Wildlife Management Area: Cartecay River Tract, Georgia
trailData.description: This route starts off Holland Cir and takes you along WMA Road and River Loop Trail in the Rich Mountain Wildlife Management Area. The trail also takes you along the Cartecay River, giving you some nice views of the water. This area has a variety of wildlife, like deer, beer, and turkeys. It's a multi-use trail popular with hikers, runners and bikers.

trailData.name: Laurel Point Loop
trailData.description: Laurel Point Loop is a beautiful wooded trail where you can enjoy solitude in peaceful surroundings. There are some opportunities for overlooks. It can be easy to get off the track because there is a paved sidewalk next to the trail. There is plenty of parking in this area, which also has picnic tables, ball fields, and bathrooms, but the bathrooms can be closed seasonally.

trailData.name: Berry Reservoir Trail
trailData.description: An offline map is recommended as users have reported that the trails are not marked well. This trail winds around the picturesque Berry Reservoir, providing lovely views of the water and surrounding forest. Along the way, you'll enjoy the shade of tall trees, spot local wildlife, and maybe even catch a glimpse of the resident deer that call the preserve home.

trailData.name: Benton MacKaye Trail: APD Hwy to Boardtown Rd
trailData.description: This day-hike section leads from the Craddock Center along the APD Highway to Boardtown Road. There are several street crossing along the way along roads with minimal traffic. While the trail passes by neighborhoods, there are still many great opportunities to observe the local wildlife in the area.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Lookout Mountain Bluff Trail
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Georgia
trailData.description: Lookout Mountain Bluff Trail offers beautiful views of the bluff. As you can guess from the trail name, there are some arrow ledges/drop off along the path, which need extra caution. The trail is well-marked, so it is easy to navigate. The last half mile back is straight up. You can find the starting point by searching 'Ochs Gateway Trailhead' on Google Maps, which is behind Covenant College.

trailData.name: Caney Creek Preserve Trail
trailData.description: Caney Creek Preserve trail is a natural surface trail within a designated 63-acre green space and transverses both woodland and pasture areas. The trail also has an interpretive segment that runs along a portion of Caney Creek. Caney Creek is a shallow, meandering stream with some shoals. There is a spot along the creek that children and dogs can access to play. Benches are available along the trail, and there is a hilltop overlook on the south end. Restrooms are available at both park...

trailData.name: Medlock Bridge Trail
trailData.location_label: Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area, Georgia
trailData.description: The Medlock Bridge Trail in Georgia offers a lovely walk through the wooded areas and along scenic creekside paths. The trail follows the Chattahoochee River, providing a mix of shaded sections and open views of the water. It’s a straightforward route, perfect for a quick walk, with a few scenic overlooks.

trailData.name: Noontootla Creek
trailData.description:
Plan ahead and Prepare—this route is not a Forest Service system trail and is not maintained for public access. Visitors should be aware that they are likely to encounter adverse conditions and do so at their own risk.

Starting at the trailhead, the Noontootla Creek Trail follows the creek for much of its length, offering numerous opportunities to appreciate the natural beauty of the surrounding forest and water. The trail winds through dense areas filled with pines, oaks, and rhododendrons,...

trailData.name: Birmingham Park Loop
trailData.description: This route takes you on a nice trail in the Birmingham Park area. You will enjoy a shaded hike and see a few old abandoned structures. You might see people riding their horses, so make sure you share the trail with others. The trails are not very well marked, so downloading the route beforehand is recommended.

trailData.name: Blue Blazes Trail
trailData.description: The Blue Blazes Trail, located in the Moccasin Bend National Archeological District, traverses wooded areas and wetlands, offering a scenic overlook of the Tennessee River. The trail can have some puddles because it goes through a swamp, but wooden planks are laid out here and there. There is a small parking area at the trailhead.

trailData.name: Project Chimps Nature Trail
trailData.description: The Nature Trail at Project Chimps is easy to stroll with little elevation change and sturdy bridges and steps. Perfect for all hiking levels! Visit the koi pond and learn about native flora and fauna along the path with 34 interpretive educational signs. Visit several times of year to see the seasonal changes in the plant life and check off different migrating bird species. Some parking is available directly at the trail head and overflow parking can be found on Lowery just west of the main...

trailData.name: Suwanee Creek Park Loop
trailData.description: The Suwanee Creek Park Loop offers visitors a scenic journey through the park's natural beauty. This well-maintained trail meanders through lush forests and open meadows, providing ample opportunities to spot wildlife. The park also features amenities such as picnic areas and restrooms, enhancing the overall experience for visitors. Whether you're interested in hiking, birdwatching, running, or simply enjoying a peaceful walk, this trail is a great option in the area.

trailData.name: Shirley Miller Wildflower Trail
trailData.location_label: Crockford-Pigeon Mountain Wildlife Management Area, Georgia
trailData.description: This route takes you from Pocket Trailhead along a nice wooden path surrounded by beautiful wildflowers to a stunning waterfall. The trail takes you along Pocket Branch, where you will enjoy the sights and sounds of the water and, at the end, the amazing waterfalls. The waterfalls' power depends on the time of year.

trailData.name: Green Meadows Preserve Loop
trailData.description: Along the way, the trail passes small creeks and ponds, where you can often spot wildlife such as birds, frogs, and small mammals. The preserve is also an excellent spot for birdwatching, with many species migrating through the area, especially during the spring and fall. The area is also home to numerous wildflower species, and the spring and summer months bring vibrant bursts of color to the landscape.

trailData.name: Blankets Creek MTB Loop
trailData.description:
The direction that you will need to ride Mosquito Bite, Van Michael, Dwelling Loop and South Loop trails change daily. Su/Mon/Wed/Fri are clockwise. Tue/Thurs/Sat are counter-clockwise. 
This mountain biking trail takes you through a great tour of Blankets Creek Park; it's easy to follow and interesting throughout for all levels of riders with bigger jumps or ride-arounds.

trailData.name: Yonah Preserve Trails: Cherokee Trail (Section 100)
trailData.description: The Cherokee Trail Section of the Yonah Preserve Trails in Georgia is a popular route for mountain bikers, offering a combination of technical terrain and scenic views. This trail features fast-paced sections with rocky climbs, tight turns, and smooth descents through dense forest. Riders can enjoy a mix of singletrack and moderate elevation changes, making it ideal for bikers looking to challenge their skills. This trail is also popular for hikers and explore the forest here, be careful...

trailData.name: Roberts Lake Trail
trailData.description:
This is a nice trail to an old dam and power plant. The trailhead can be hard to find. Apple/Google Maps can navigate you to the incorrect starting point. You can drive/bike like you are following directions to The Wheeler House. Turn into Roberts Lake Road, drop down that single lane road until it turns into a gravel road. 4x4 is best on this road. Keep going until you see the sign. Parking is a small gravel lot. 

The "moderate" difficulty rating on this trail is due to the up-and-down...

trailData.name: Piedmont Park Family-Friendly Walk
trailData.description:
This 189 acre park has playgrounds, a pool, nature activities, dog park and more for serendipitous family fun.

Atlanta's Piedmont Park is located about two miles Northeast of Downtown Atlanta on 189 acres. It is adjacent to the Atlanta Botanical Gardens and along the Atlanta BeltLine. The park has a storied history. The space was the site of exhibitions, a World's Fair, professional baseball games and the first football match up between Southern rivals University of Georgia and Auburn...

trailData.name: Martins Mine, Cathy Ellis and Ash Creek Trail
trailData.description: The trail offers a relaxing walk on well-maintained trails. Most of the time, you will walk on a paved path with some gravel paths, too. On the way to the waterfall at the end, there are a couple of river crossings. Smithgall Woods Visitors Center has a small museum that you can check out to learn about the nature and history of the surrounding areas.

trailData.name: Clayton County International Park
trailData.description: This is a superb trail in Clayton County International Park. Visitors can expect beautiful views, workout equipment along the path, and a scenic environment with lakes and bridges. The path is made of asphalt and concrete and offers a good mix of shade and sun. The elevation changes also provide an excellent workout. Access the trail from the parking area on the eastern side of Indian Lake.

trailData.name: Beech Bottom Trail
trailData.description:
Beech Bottom Trail is primarily used as an access trail for day hikes to Jacks River Falls. The trail is easy to follow, wide, and has mild inclines and declines. There are several spots on the trail where you can get a scenic view of the Jacks River valley, making it a highly recommended hike. 

The Beech Bottom/Jacks River Falls area is open for day use only from April 1st through October 31st each year.

trailData.area_name: Reflection Riding Arboretum and Nature Center
trailData.name: Reflection Riding Arboretum Lookout Creek Trail
trailData.location_label: Reflection Riding Arboretum and Nature Center, Tennessee
trailData.description: Reflection Riding Arboretum & Nature Center is open to the public for free Tuesday through Saturday each week, but relies on the support of members and the community to operate. If you are a member, please proceed to the member or main parking lots and place your membership card on your dashboard. If you are a visitor, please reserve a visit pass  (https://reflectionriding.org/plan-your-visit) and park in the main parking lot.

trailData.name: Terrapin Cove Trail
trailData.description: This route takes you through the Don Carter State Park area along a well-maintained trail on a mostly flat trail with pleasant hills. This trail takes you along the shore of the Chattahoochee River with lovely waterfront views as you go, creating a very peaceful atmosphere for your hike. Some of the trails have exposed roots, so sturdy shoes are recommended.

trailData.name: Johnson Ferry Short Loop
trailData.description:
A wide path along the Chattahoochee River used for walking. There are two different trails with different parking areas and starting points. Johnson Ferry South and North. This is the South loop.

From the parking lot if you go west it becomes a very narrow path that leads through a nice forest and ends up on private property. To the east, it is a very wide path along the river that leads to the now-closed second parking lot.

trailData.name: Hard Labor Creek Blue Trail
trailData.location_label: Hard Labor Creek State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This is the prettiest of the three main trails and the most popular with hikers and trail runners, as well as families on bikes.  Two very pretty cascading creeks offer several picnic areas to enjoy a day in the woods.  There are several short challenging sections that also have shortcut trails that allow beginners a bail-out option.

trailData.name: Appalachian Trail: Hightower Gap to Gooch Shelter
trailData.description: The Hightower Gap to Gooch Shelter trail is a scenic section of the Appalachian Trail in Georgia. Hikers will experience a variety of terrain, including forests and rocky outcrops. The trail offers beautiful wilderness views and the opportunity to spot wildlife. It is well-marked with white blazes, making navigation straightforward. The Gooch Mountain Shelter, provides a great resting spot. Some sections may have limited water access, so planning ahead is recommended. This trail is popular...

trailData.name: Panola Mountain Visitors Center to South River Trail
trailData.description: Outside of the city sits Panola Mountain State Park, a beautiful 1300-acre area that is great for hiking, biking, fishing and camping. The park has the most beautiful scenery in Georgia and takes visitors outside of the bustle of city life. Hikers will enjoy the diverse scenery which includes mountains, streams, and wildlife. There is a wide variety of trail networks.

trailData.name: Talking Rock Jon's Trail
trailData.description: This is an easy trail for beginner mountain biking, which is smooth and a fun flow trail. This trail is intended to be multi-use and is shared by mountain bikers and hikers. There are gradual climbs and descents located on this route and many agree that this is one of the best trails in the area to begin. There are other trails in this park to connect to for those who wish to extend their hike.

trailData.name: Chicopee Backcountry Trail
trailData.description:
This route follows a winding path through the woods that reveals a diverse set of forest types.  There are multiple creek crossings and steep terrain changes throughout the route, making this route a must do for hikers looking for a bit more challenge.  This route can be combined with other routes to create a loop or simply follow the route back to the parking lot. 

This trail is designated for for hiking, birding and pedestrian use only. No mountain biking is allowed. 

As of January 1,...

trailData.name: High Point
trailData.location_label: Crockford-Pigeon Mountain Wildlife Management Area, Georgia

trailData.name: Sea Creek Falls
trailData.description:
Plan ahead and Prepare—this route is not a Forest Service system trail and is not maintained for public access. Visitors should be aware that they are likely to encounter adverse conditions and do so at their own risk.

This is a marvelous trail to Sea Creek Falls in Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest. This area is a well-known swimming spot, so expect to see other visitors enjoying the falls and swimming area. The hike starts from the Sea Creek Trail parking area located at the end of Sea...

trailData.name: Garrard Landing Park Loop
trailData.description:
The Garrard Landing Park Loop primarily has a gravel surface. The ½ mile segment along the Chattahoochee River is fully shaded and has an observation deck. The rest of the trail meanders through an open meadow and features a man-made lake, cascading stream, covered bridge, and pond. There are several interconnecting segments that allow customization of the length.

Accessibility: 

Equipment
Visitors using wheelchairs, mobility equipment, or strollers may need all-terrain tires or...

trailData.name: Brantley and Beaverpond Nature Trails
trailData.location_label: Hard Labor Creek State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: Brantley and Beaverpond Nature Trails is a great and serene trail to meander around in the woods. The trail is well-maintained and easy to follow with signage. There are some features that make your hike more interesting, such as a pond, wood bridge, and creek. There is plenty of parking at the trailhead.

trailData.name: Line Creek to Lake Mac Trail
trailData.description: This easygoing trail begins from the parking lot at the end of Line Creek Drive. It's a beautiful hike that meanders along Line Creek to the lake and back again. You'll want sturdy shoes for this one, as there are many exposed tree roots and rocks to navigate. There are benches along the way where you can stop to soak up the views of the creek.

trailData.name: Nature Trail
trailData.description: Natural Trailhead is a great family trail to enjoy a short natural walk. It features small creek crossings and bridges. The trail has a very slight change in elevation, making it perfect for people of all ages. There are lots of trees along the way, providing a great amount of shade. At the beginning of the trail is Harold Cox Nature Garden, which has many different plants and informative signs.

trailData.name: Bull Mountain, Jones Creek, Moss Creek, and Jake Mountain Loop
trailData.description: This trail is a beautiful multi-use path that winds through a shaded forest. It is a popular route for mountain biking enthusiasts in the area. There are two small streams to cross, and your feet might get wet depending on the water flow. Although there are no scenic viewpoints along the way, there is a possibility of spotting some wildlife.

trailData.name: Can't Hardly Loop
trailData.description: Although many trails in this area are mountain biker friendly, the Can't Hardly trail is hikers only. This trail is well marked. It’s hard to describe the beauty and fun of this wonderful trail. It winds through a lush, beautiful and densely forested area. The creek runs close to the trail in many spots with a number of easy walk-downs which would be great for exploring and cooling-off; in other areas the creek can only be heard as it is far below in deep and beautiful ravines.

trailData.name: Gwinnett Environmental Heritage Center Trails
trailData.description:
The 233-acre GEHC has its own trail system and links up to the Ivy Creek Greenway.  Its 8-mile network of hard and soft trails allows exploration of the stream and forest habitats and is suitable for walking, running, hiking, and biking. Trails are open from dusk to dawn and year-round.

There are 11 trails that are constructed of a variety of hard and soft surfaces.  Individual trail difficulty runs from easy to strenuous and lengths of .05 to 1 mile.

Accessibility: Visitors using...

trailData.name: Dockery Lake Trail
trailData.description:
This route starts you at Dockery Lake Trailhead and takes you on an enjoyable incline with some rocky and steep sections. The path along the lake is very peaceful and provides some nice waterfront views. You have the option to continue on the trail along the east side of the lake as well. 

Note: The forest service road to this trail may be closed in winter. Be prepared to add a two-mile round trip to this distance.

trailData.name: Collins Hill Park
trailData.location_label: Collins Hill Road County Park, Georgia
trailData.description: Collins Hill Road County Park is a great place to meander around and it is a popular spot for children and families to be outdoors and enjoy nature. The trail offers a nice and casual walk through the woods with plenty of shade. It is wide gravel and dirt path with a minimum incline. When you reach the lake, you can enjoy beautiful and peaceful views.

trailData.name: Yellow River Equestrian South Loop
trailData.description:
Yellow River Park features a multi-user trail system where users can travel in either direction on their designated trails. Bicycles must yield to hikers, while both bicycles and hikers should yield to equestrians, ensuring a safe and enjoyable experience for everyone.
This lovely trail explores the beautiful Yellow River Park. It offers great forest walking and views of the river throughout.

trailData.name: Matt Park Trail
trailData.description: Matt Park in Georgia features a network of trails perfect for a leisurely hike or nature walk. The park offers scenic views of the surrounding landscape, with well-maintained paths winding through wooded areas, meadows, and open spaces. It’s an ideal spot for families, beginners, or anyone looking to enjoy a peaceful escape into nature.

trailData.name: Toccoa River Trail via Benton MacKaye Duncan Ridge Trail
trailData.description: This hiking loop starts at the Benton Mackaye Trailhead, which is located near Highway 60. The trail follows the river and passes through the woods, offering stunning views of the mountains from the ridge line. Eventually, it leads to the famous swinging bridge, and from there, it follows the forest service road back to Highway 60.

trailData.name: Cochran Mill Loop 1
trailData.description: This route takes you around part of Cochran Mill Park on a nice trail with enjoyable hills. You can enjoy fantastic views of Little Bear Creek with a beautiful multitier waterfall off the creek. It also takes you to Bear Creek, where you can enjoy more water views. This area can get slick, so sturdy shoes are recommended.

trailData.name: Hardwood Forest, Pine Forest, Beaver Pond, and Creek Loop
trailData.description: Clyde Shepherd Nature is home to diverse wildlife like foxes, turtles, and various birds. It has several different trail systems to explore, most offering peaceful natural walks. The loop also has some benches and observation decks. There are places to rest at the trailhead: a pavilion, benches, and a small garden.

trailData.name: White’s Mill Park Loop
trailData.description: This park has been renovated from the historic milling site of a Georgia settler. What was once a grain production area, is now a place for neighboring communities to recreate outdoors. The park sits alongside Cedar Creek and offers a peaceful walk through a forested area. There is interpretive signage throughout the trail to educate visitors on the history in this place.

trailData.name: Big Haynes Creek Nature Center Blue Trail Loop
trailData.description:
Enjoy this great trail using Blue Blazes that explore this lovely park, make sure to stay on the blue path as the Red Trail is a mountain biking route only (one direction only). This trail explores woodland, ponds and open fields and makes for a great hike, run, dog walk or cycle. 

The Georgia International Horse Park has the first-ever Olympic mountain biking course in the world! For more information on the park, please visit:...

trailData.name: Autrey Mill Nature Preserve Trail
trailData.description:
Autrey Mill Nature Preserve includes two miles of walking trails (some mulched) that wind past a creek with rocky shoals, spring seeps, mature trees, wildflowers, native plants, and a variety of animal life.

The trail winds down to a ravine, follows along Sal's creek, and then turns and goes back up in elevation to the start at the heritage village.  The trail is mulched in places and can be traverse by people in a fair state of fitness, but is not set up for people with disabilities.

trailData.name: Roswell Area Park Orange Loop
trailData.description: This route takes you along a predominantly soft surface with lights around the trail if you want to hike around the Roswell Area Park perimeter at night. It is mostly shaded, encompasses a fishing lake, and crosses a creek. At the lake, you'll most likely see some ducks or other types of birds, and there are plenty of benches around, making for a wonderful break spot on your hike.

trailData.name: Browns Mill Battlefield Blue Blaze Trail
trailData.description: This route takes you around the historic Browns Mill Battlefield, where you will enjoy some nice elevation change on a well-maintained trail. Historic information signs along the way help you appreciate the importance of this area. Several trails connect, making it easy to extend your hike but harder to navigate, so make sure you download the route beforehand.

trailData.name: Ivy Terrace Trail
trailData.description: Ivy Terrace Park, near downtown Gainesville, has nice urban trail systems with natural settings that are family-friendly. At the beginning of the trail, there is a large kid's playground, a pavilion with grills, and a bathroom. The trail is paved and mostly shaded, with streams meandering through the paths.

trailData.name: Appalachian Trail: Unicoi Gap to Chattahoochee Gap
trailData.description: This route follows a section of the famous Appalachian Trail, starting from the Unicoi Gap and ending at the Chattahoochee Gap. Along the way you will enjoy some stunning views as you take on a challenging incline with some steep and rocky sections along the way. You will pass by Blue Mountain, Red, Spaniards Knob, and Jacks Knob.

trailData.name: Marble Mine Trail to Pinhoti Trail
trailData.location_label: James H. (Sloppy) Floyd State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This trail leads hikers along a former road to an abandoned marble mine, featuring a 35-foot waterfall cascading over a marble outcrop into a reflective pool. The path is relatively easy, making it suitable for families and casual hikers. Along the way, visitors can observe remnants of the area's mining history and enjoy the surrounding natural beauty. The trail connects to a larger network, offering opportunities for extended hikes.

trailData.area_name: Garland Mountain Horse and Hiking Trails
trailData.name: Garland Mountain: East Side Loop
trailData.location_label: Garland Mountain Horse and Hiking Trails, Georgia
trailData.description: This route takes you along Palomino, Sorrel, and Greenway East, where you'll cross several creeks. Sometimes, the trails can be hard to follow, so downloading the route before you go will make it easier to follow. This is a multi-use trail, and you'll generally see some horses on the trail, so make sure to show proper trail etiquette.

trailData.name: Helen and Bottoms Loop
trailData.description: This trail overlaps with the beginning of the route from Unicoi to Helen but soon branches off to create this loop. It's a pleasant and easy hike, primarily situated in shaded areas with a section by the creek, making it a great choice for a comfortable outdoor experience. If you wish to extend your hike, there are many trails to the west of this trail.

trailData.name: Laurel Falls from Lost Falls Trailhead
trailData.description: This route takes you from the Lost Falls Trailhead on a steady incline along Orange Trail to Lost Falls and Laurel Falls. Both waterfalls offer a unique experience, making them must-sees along the trail. The trail is well-maintained, with some rocky and slick spots, so proper footwear is recommended for this hike.

trailData.name: Benton MacKaye Trail: Bushy Head Gap to Watson Gap
trailData.description: This trail has no specific destination and is great for a secluded hike through the woods. The trail is well-marked and has some climb, which would make a good exercise. You can start the hike by following the small dirt path that runs alongside the road from the starting point. There is no designated parking lot.

trailData.name: Rolling Green and Dogwood Loop
trailData.location_label: White Oak Mountain Trail System, Tennessee
trailData.description: This route starts from the parking lot on Morningside Dr. and takes you along Rolling Green and Dogwood trails in the White Oak Mountain area. It is a steady and enjoyable incline along a well-maintained trail. Several trails connect to this route, so you have plenty of options if you want to extend your hike.

trailData.name: Freeman Trail
trailData.description: The Freeman Trail in Georgia offers a peaceful and scenic hike through the Blood Mountain Wilderness. As part of the Appalachian Trail system, this trail passes through diverse landscapes, including woodlands and rocky outcrops. Hikers can enjoy views of the surrounding forests and mountainous terrain, making it a great spot for nature lovers looking to immerse themselves in the beauty of Georgia’s wilderness.  This is a great trail with campsites and restrooms on trail.

trailData.name: Nitro North, South and John’s Corner Trail
trailData.description: The Nitro North and South trails feature smooth, winding paths through towering hardwoods and pine forests, with occasional rocky sections and gentle climbs that keep the trail engaging for all skill levels. The John’s Corner Trail adds an extra loop of adventure, weaving through quiet wooded areas with small creek crossings and wildlife sightings. The well-maintained trails offer excellent footing, making them ideal for fast-paced trail running or a relaxed nature hike.

trailData.name: Lackey Road Greenspace Loop
trailData.description: The Lackey Road Greenspace is a 1.5-mile wooded trail through a 106-acre property the City purchased in 2018 as part of the Greenspace Bond. This picturesque property - formerly the Wolff property - set off a rural gravel road features winding, rolling trails in southwest Milton. Starting at a gravel parking lot that holds about 15 cars, visitors walk alongside (and, in some cases, over) bubbling creeks, watch cows munching in an adjoining pasture, traverse through dense forest, and enjoy...

trailData.name: Mosquito Flats and Mosquito Bite Loop
trailData.description: These loops are multi-use, but they are primarily designed for mountain biking. The trail system is one-way, ensuring safe flow for riders. The trailhead at Blankets Creek offers ample parking, restrooms, picnic tables, and a bike repair station. The trails are open year-round, but they may close temporarily after rain to prevent damage.

trailData.name: Mount Tabor Blue Trail
trailData.description: This is a relaxing trail with almost no elevation in the woods. The trail is mostly dirt with lots of shades. You will cross over a small wood bridge and get to the pond. There are many intersecting trails, so it can be challenging to find the trail you intend to hike, so download the map ahead of time.

trailData.name: Duncan Ridge Trail to Blood Mountain
Jack's Knob Trail from Jack's Gap to Chattahoochee River Headwaters
trailData.description: Jack's Knob Trail is a moderately challenging hike that starts at Jack's Gap, located near Brasstown Bald, Georgia's highest peak. This trail takes you through dense hardwood forests, along ridges, and offers occasional scenic views of the surrounding Blue Ridge Mountains. The trail has a steady ascent, with some steep sections, making it a good workout for experienced hikers.

trailData.name: Central Loop Trail
trailData.description: The trail is multi-use but is especially favored by mountain bikers in the area. The terrain is mostly flat, providing plenty of shade and lovely views of the lake. The trail is well-maintained and marked and passes through a forest with lush greenery. There are also intersecting trails for those who wish to explore off the main path.

trailData.name: Sara Babb Park Trail
trailData.description: There is a small side trail on the southeastern side of the loop that goes partially up Ray Mountain.

trailData.name: Eagle's Beak Trail
trailData.description:
Enjoy this lovely trail through Eagles Beak Park as it heads through the forest and past Etoway River. 

For information on park hours, please visit: https://parks.forsythco.com/Parks/Eagles-Beak-Park 

This park also offers other amenities, such as a Canoe/kayak launch, picnic tables and restrooms.

trailData.name: Wilscot Gap to Brawley Mountain Loop
trailData.description:
This trail starts where the Benton Mackaye Trail crosses Ga Hwy 60. There is parking for about 8 cars at the trailhead. The trail follows Benton MacKaye approximately 3.2 miles to the top of Brawley Mountain, where there is an old Fire Tower, which is now being used as a communications tower. The top of the tower is not accessible. 

The hike starts out on a rather steep grade. The elevation gain in the first mile is about 645 feet then it levels out as you summit Tipton Mountain. The trail...

trailData.name: Dogwood, Rolling Green, Valley and Pine Loop
trailData.location_label: White Oak Mountain Trail System, Tennessee

trailData.name: Cashes Valley Road
trailData.description: Cashes Valley Road is a route that is mainly used for off-road driving. It is along a private residential area, and the trail is gated at the end, so you have to turn around. But you can still have fun, crossing several beautiful streams. The trail is in great shape overall. There are several cabins near the start if you are interested.

trailData.name: East Mulberry Equestrian and Ravine Loop Trail
Laurel Loop
trailData.description: This shared-use trail travels vertically (south then north) through the park with a handful of tight turns, small rock jumps, and several creek crossings. This is a relatively easy trail with a gradual downhill and little climbing. The trail is well-maintained with an easy-to-follow layout and signage. The tight turns are often bermed and the trail is lined with tall hardwoods.

trailData.name: Explorer Trail
trailData.description:
All trails here are directional by day of the week. The directions below are for mountain biking. If hiking/running, go the OPPOSITE way of the bikers!

Sun/Mon/Wed/Fri Clockwise or to the left
Tue/Thu/Sat  Counter-Clockwise or to the right

The trails here:
Explorer (~3.5 miles total; dirt)
Avalanche (~6.25 miles total; dirt)
The Mill (~5.1 miles total; dirt)
Trestle Rock (~.5 mile; paved)

Each dirt trail is made up of loops that are "stacked" so you can choose your mileage. Mtn bikes have...

trailData.name: Black Shoals Nature and Scenic Trail
trailData.location_label: Big Haynes Creek Rec Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
This route travels through the woods and across a beautiful granite outcropping. After a short hike along the highway, the trail leads over to the lake via a covered bridge. Explore the scenic woodlands year-round and experience the beauty that this park offers.

The park is open from 8am-6pm and closed on Wednesdays.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Chickamauga Ramble Trail
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Georgia

trailData.name: The Ridge Red and Yellow Loop
trailData.description: This is the inner loop at The Ridge Nature Area park. This route travels by a river early on and has slight declines/ inclines. This is a great choice for the whole family to enjoy! There are not many views along the trail, however, there are many opportunities to view wildlife and wildflowers. If you are looking for a longer route, check out the perimeter trail in the park.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Colquitt Monument and Helm Monument Loop
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Georgia

trailData.name: White Oak Mountain Big Red Trail Loop
trailData.location_label: White Oak Mountain Trail System, Tennessee
trailData.description: This route starts at the Red Loop Trailhead at Morningside Drive within the University. This trail is mainly a mountain biker trail but also welcomes foot traffic, so stay alert while on the path. The trail is well-maintained and takes you along some enjoyable hills. Wildlife is also found in this area, so watch for that.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Upper Truck Trail, Bluff, Mountain Beautiful and Hardy Trail Loop
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Tennessee
trailData.description: This route starts on Upper Truck Trail with an intense incline to reach Sunset Rock, then levels out. At Sunset Rock, you'll see a giant boulder that gives you panoramic views of the Lookout Mountain Area. Sometimes, that last mile or so of the trail can be overgrown, so it's best to be prepared with long pants.

trailData.name: Eagle's Rest Trail at Mount Oglethorpe
trailData.description: Mount Oglethorpe offers very nice views in all directions, from multiple observation decks. This trail winds through lush forests and rocky outcrops, offering several observation points along the way. At the summit of Mount Oglethorpe, hikers are rewarded with breathtaking vistas of the surrounding landscape.

trailData.name: Zahnd Wildlife Area Loop
trailData.description: This is not a state-sanctioned trail, and the route may be difficult to navigate in certain areas. It is recommended to download the offline map ahead of time.

trailData.name: Gibbs Garden Fern Dell Route
trailData.description:
This is one of many routes/trails you can walk in the Gibbs Gardens. To reach the Fern Dell trail, you must travel through the entrance, the Waterlily Gardens, and then finally through the Japanese Garden. The Fern Dell is a short circular route. The GPS map attached follow this path.

The route itself is very easy difficulty and can be completed with a stroller. Enjoy the wonderful views of the first two gardens and then the serenity of the Fern Dell. 

Accessibility: There are at least 5...

trailData.name: Mumbo Jummbo, Voodoo and Hocus Pocus Loop
trailData.description:
These mountain biking trails are well-marked and well-maintained, although there are sections with roots and mud. There is a great variety of trail options to choose from in this park, but most are rated as difficult.
For more information on the park, please visit: https://mtbatlanta.com/allatoona-creek-park/

trailData.name: Williams Mill Greenspace Perimeter Loop
trailData.description: Williams Mill Greenspace trail network has over 2 miles of trails within a nature preserve that protects 48 acres of rolling hills, streams, ponds and wildlife. The Greenspace is certified as a Wildlife Sanctuary with the Atlanta Audubon Society.  The trail includes asphalt, dirt, and grass surfaces and spans both meadows and woodland. Mitchell Creek winds through the park and drops in elevation as it cascades over granite shoals. The scenic park is a favorite among professional photographers.

trailData.name: Bull Sluice Lake
trailData.description: The left part of the loop that starts around the playground/pavilion area is an easy walk. Right side that starts behind the Paddle Shack is ok at first, then gets very narrow (cleared trail often goes down to 1ft in width) with lots of roots and overgrown plants on the side. Long pants and good shoes recommended.

trailData.name: Arabia Mountain from Panola Mountain Visitor Center
Cochran Creek Falls
trailData.description:
There are a few small clearings for parking but no designated parking area or trailhead. If you have a 4x4 vehicle you can cross the creek and park in the camping area.

Users have reported that this can be a rough route as it is on a narrow path that is not marked well and there is a lot of scrambling in the last half-mile especially. Fallen trees occur regularly.

trailData.name: Tray Mountain from Tray Gap via Appalachian Trail
Pinhoti Trail: GA 136 to Mill Creek Mountain

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Chickamauga Battlefield Hunt Cemetery
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Georgia

trailData.name: Fightingtown Creek Loop
trailData.description: This shared-use trail meanders through rolling hills and tall hardwoods. This trail gradually declines for most of the duration with a bit of a climb toward the end. There are some tight turns and several creek crossings but there are not too many technical maneuvers making for a beginner-intermediate mountain bike ride.

trailData.name: Silver Comet Trail from Coots Lake
Pinhoti Trail: Mulberry Gap Road to Cohutta Overlook
Black Mountain Fire Tower
trailData.description:
You have to park at Woody Gap and then walk north about 150 yards along the side of the road to access the trail. Exercise caution, as the road shoulders can be narrow in places.

This is a very rocky service road that has seen better days, and quite steep in some areas. At the top you are rewarded with a great panoramic view. There is also an old fire tower that has been converted into an antenna farm that houses an amateur (ham) radio repeater and Camp Merrill backup phone radio system,...

trailData.name: Mason's Connector to Mason's Bridge Loop
Byron Herbert Reese Nature Trail
trailData.description: This route takes you along an easy trail with some steep sections on steps next to the rental cabins in the Vogel State Park area. The trail is well-marked and has educational signs along the way. This hike is great for kids and adults alike and worth the trip. The fall is a great time to visit when the leaves change color.

trailData.name: Jackrabbit Mountain Loop
trailData.description: This trail is designed for both mountain bikers and hikers to use. It includes some hilly and challenging sections, so make sure you're ready. Remember to bring bug repellent, as there can be a lot of bugs, especially during the summer. Take in the stunning lake views along the way and enjoy your hike or bike ride!

trailData.name: Oglethorpe Mt. Trail
trailData.description: To get to the Eagle's Eye Picnic Area, start from the main parking lot and follow the trail marked with yellow blazes. As you proceed, you will enter a dense and beautiful forest and reach the old CCC logging road. Keep following the road, and you will come across the Mountain Stewards picnic area before eventually returning to the trailhead. The trail has its fair share of ups and downs, but the stunning views towards the end make it all worth it.

trailData.name: Meadow, Woodland, and Purple Mark Loop
trailData.description: The loop around the lake will take you through the front yard of an abandoned house, and part of the that trail has caution tape because the river crossing is a small bit treacherous. Just before you get to the lake there is a pretty cool rock outcropping.

trailData.name: Rolling Green, The Fall, Krebs Cycle and Dogwood Loop
trailData.location_label: White Oak Mountain Trail System, Tennessee

trailData.name: Benton MacKaye Trail: Dyer Gap to Flat Top Mountain
Turner Lake Trail
trailData.description:
Nature is Turner Lake Park's biggest draw. The setting is as serene as any you'll find. The walking trails provide a scenic place to exercise, with Turner Lake, a local landmark, as its backdrop. The trails are supplied with numerous benches where people can take a break from walking to sit down and enjoy the park's incredible views.

Accessibility:

Equipment  
Visitors using wheelchairs, mobility equipment, or strollers may need all-terrain tires or adaptive/motorized equipment for the...

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Bluff, John Smartt, and Upper Truck Trail Loop
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Tennessee
trailData.description: This is a good loop from Cravens House that is relatively easy and should only take a few hours to do. It’s a good trail for any time of year, but during the summer keep your eyes peeled for snakes. If you do the side trip up to Sunset Rock you can get a good view of Lookout Valley amd Raccoon Mountain.

trailData.name: Boyd Gap to Brush Creek Trail
Benton MacKaye and Shallowford Bridge Rd Loop
trailData.description: The trailhead for this route starts along Shallowford Bridge Rd and takes the Benton MacKaye trailhead by the Toccoa River. A spur trail along this way leads to Free Knob for those wishing to add more distance to their hike. The route finishes by looping back onto Shallowford Road and returns to the parking lot.

trailData.name: Beltline Northside Trail
trailData.description: This trail sits on the north side of Atlanta winding through Tanyard Creek Park. It offers visitors the most picturesque views which includes a CSV railroad trestle. Even though this trail is still in the city, hikers will feel a sense of comfortable solitude in nature. The trail runs next to the Bobby Jones Golf Course and is great for hiking, running, or biking.

trailData.name: Pickett's Mill Red, White, and Blue Trail Loop
E.E. Robinson Nature Trail
trailData.location_label: E E Robinson Memorial Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
This trail is one of two trails within E.E. Robinson Park. This natural surface trail is located within the woodlands of the park’s Football Complex.  It can be accessed by using the sidewalk connector near the tennis courts.  The trail runs along a wooded ravine which was formed by a meandering and cascading creek.  The trail crosses the creek at multiple points by a bridge.

Accessibility: There are 9 designated accessible spaces in the paved parking lot off of Peachtree Industrial...

trailData.name: Elwyn John Wildlife Sanctuary
trailData.description: Elwyn John Loop Trail is a wide and easy path around the preserve. There is a viewing and sitting platform overlooking the area, with a view of a creek and a tiny waterfall. At the start, a nice open meadow also makes for a good picnic area. A longer extension leads uphill and connects to one of the neighborhoods.

trailData.name: Georgia Nuclear Aircraft Laboratory Block House
trailData.location_label: Dawson Forest Wildlife Management Area, Georgia

trailData.name: Dog Creek Inner and Outer Loop
trailData.description: The Dog Creek Trail at Don Carter is part of the equestrian trail system but the system is also open to foot traffic. The loop has a few steep climbs. There are three or four spots where a bridge crosses the creek. Lots of wildlife.

trailData.name: Sutallee Trace White, Orange, and Purple Loop
Jacks River Trail to Beech Bottom
trailData.description:
If you're looking for an unforgettable hike through the Georgia wilderness, consider starting in Alaculsey and embarking on a 3-day backpacking trip up the entire Jacks River Trail. One of the most unique aspects of this hike is the 22 river crossings (one-way), which can be challenging due to the swift current and slippery rocks. 

It is recommended to bring trekking poles or find a sturdy walking stick to help navigate the crossings. If you're looking to camp, there's an excellent spot past...

trailData.name: Burnt Mountain Preserve Trail
trailData.description:
The Burnt Mt. Preserve, a county-owned 900 acre Preserve, begins at the 2,500 foot elevation on the southern border along Rt 136 and extends southward toward Grandview Lake. The land drops off steeply to the south into Champion Creek valley in the bottom land of the Preserve.

The Preserve Trail begins at the parking lot and loops through the upper portion of the western section of the Preserve. The trail is rated Moderate. The trail after dropping down through about 150 feet of elevation...

trailData.name: Lake Zwerner Upper Loop
trailData.description:
This trail travels along the eastern banks of the Lake and climbs into the hills amongst a thick timber canopy with beautiful lake and mountain views. 
There are some challenging areas where the trail gets steep (50%). The trail north of the north parking area is gravel. The Lake is popular for fishing from the shore and by boat.  You will see canoes, kayaks and paddleboards.

trailData.name: Pigeon Mountain via Rocktown Trail
trailData.location_label: Crockford-Pigeon Mountain Wildlife Management Area, Georgia
trailData.description: This is a relatively flat trail that leads to a grouping of boulders known as Rock Town. Bouldering grades range from easy to difficult. Rock climbing information can be accessed at https://www.seclimbers.org/project/rocktown/

trailData.name: Appalachian Trail: Indian Grave Gap to Rocky Mountain
trailData.location_label: Swallow Creek Wildlife Management Area, Georgia

trailData.name: Brown Thrasher Trail Loop
trailData.description: This is a wonderful Georgia ridge line trail and is very well blazed and very well marked.

trailData.name: Providence Park Red and Blue Loop Trail
trailData.description: Providence Park Trail is located in a 42 acre green space in Milton, GA.  The trail primarily has a dirt surface and consists of two trail loops; each identified by either “Red” or “Blue” markings.  The Red loop (West side) features a lake.  The Blue loop (East side) features several stream crossings and overlooks a fenced-off, abandoned quarry.

trailData.name: Little River Backcountry Road
trailData.location_label: Little River Canyon National Preserve, Alabama
trailData.description:
This is a great public 4x4 trail. There are ruts, rocks, and little water crossings to make it fun. Towards the middle you can cross the river if you want, or stay left to continue on the trail. Good off-road trail for new or experienced people wanting a relaxing trail ride. Look out for horses and people if you are driving. Make sure to stay on the road and don't try to drive on the hiking trails. 

For more information, you can visit the park website: https://www.nps.gov/liri/index.htm

trailData.name: North Hall Park
trailData.description: This trail has two sections. One is a flat loop around a pasture and the other is a typical North Georgia style trail of easy to average difficulty. These trails are extremely well maintained and used frequently.

trailData.name: Pumpkinvine Creek Blue Loop
trailData.description: This is the longest trail system in Pumpkinvine Creek Nature Preserve. The route wanders through diverse areas featuring swamp land, open grassy fields, and hardwood forests. You can extend your route by adding on the green loop, located on the western side of the park. There is plenty of shade through the forested areas and many opportunities to watch wildlife in the area.

trailData.name: Burrell's Cove and Saba Beach
trailData.description:
Jackrabbit Mountain Recreation Area is situated in the Tusquitee Ranger District of the Nantahala National Forest. It is located on a wooded peninsula overlooking the picturesque 6,950-acre Lake Chatuge, with a backdrop of high mountain peaks. Lake Chatuge is acclaimed as the crown jewel of TVA's system of lakes.

The lake resembles a Swiss alpine setting and is home to a variety of fish, including spotted white, and striped bass, catfish, crappie, and sunfish.

Several sites and...

trailData.name: Jackson Hill Trail
trailData.description: Historic Jackson Hill was the location of Fort Norton, an earthen fortification system which defended Rome during the Civil War. During the Great Depression, the area was redeveloped by the Works Progress Administration, which included the Rome Civic Center, an amphitheater (now the Labyrinth of Rome), several rock bridges and more. Today, winding trails provide a quiet getaway just blocks from Downtown Rome. Outdoor exhibits include the Boswell Cabin Trailhead, a cotton gin, replicas of...

trailData.name: Charlies Creek Road
trailData.description:
This is primarily a off-road driving road but is a multi-use two-track/road in the national forest so hikers, bikers, and horseback riders are also welcome. Be aware though that you will definitely see off-roading vehicles here most days. No ATV's or UTV's allowed.

For off-road travelers there are river and creek crossings and a few rock climbs. It is 2-way traffic so be mindful of other users on the road.

trailData.name: John's Homestead Trail
trailData.description: This is a new trail in the area in a new park that is being developed by the city of Tucker and by the DeKalb County Parks Department. There’s a lot going on here and a lot of history. This was the last remaining homestead within DeKalb County so it’s a significant historical location and interesting look at the past.

trailData.name: Sutallee Trace Green Trail
trailData.description:
The Green Trail is an approximately two-mile loop that begins and ends at the New Hightower Church Parking and Trailhead. The loop begins - on both sides - in an area dubbed "no-man's land" because of the complete removal of all vegetation by the clear-cut operations. The area is starting to rejuvenate and trail markings can be found on ground posts. Because the Green initially shares the trail with the White, the trailheads are marked with a post that features blazes for both trails.

The...

trailData.name: Short Bull Trail
trailData.description: This is a very nice and peaceful hike. Users note that when Jones Creek is full, it is difficult to cross without getting wet.

trailData.name: Dogwood and White Oak Ridge Loop
trailData.location_label: White Oak Mountain Trail System, Tennessee
trailData.description: Dogwood and White Oak Ridge wind their way through the forest on family-friendly trails, with multiple other options for people who want more or less distance. With so many trails, it can get confusing at times, so pay close attention to the map as you go. It's important to remember that this is a multi-use trail and is shared with hikers and bikers.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Lower Cascades Glen Falls 65
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Tennessee

trailData.name: Murphey Candler Park Short Loop
trailData.description:
Beautiful well established trail through the woods around the lake.

This trail is very well established and easy to traverse.  There are a few small sections that include rocks and roots, but typically it is hard packed dirt or sidewalk.  Any streams, water or troublesome areas are easily traversed by way of sturdily built bridges.

trailData.name: Mineral Springs Nature Trail
trailData.description: This is a beautiful flat trail that travels through a few wooded acres of land. While short, this is a great family-friendly route that is perfect for those short on time or who wants a quick walk through the woods. While there are no longer mineral springs located here, there are informational markers to educate visitors on the history of the area.

trailData.name: Wildlife viewing
trailData.location_label: Dawson Forest Wildlife Management Area, Georgia

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Mullis Spring Loop
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Georgia
trailData.description:
This trail begins at the parking lot on the park's north border at Park City Rd and Reed's Bridge Rd (McFarland Ave). Take the unpaved Mullis Rd south and meet up with the red trail heading west until it intersects another road heading south again. Turn left at the yellow trail where you will have views of a large open field and Snodgrass House. Complete the loop by taking the green trail north to Mullis Rd.

There is a $10 fee per person to enter the park.

trailData.area_name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
trailData.name: Chickamauga Western Loop
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Georgia
trailData.description: This pathway offers a journey through a significant historical landscape within the nation's first and largest military park. As you explore, you will be heading through areas where the Battle of Chickamauga unfolded, a major engagement in the Civil War. You'll encounter numerous monuments and historical markers that tell the story of the soldiers and events that took place on these grounds. The trail meanders through a mix of forests, which can include mature trees, and open fields, where...

trailData.name: Elsie A Holmes Nature Trail
trailData.location_label: Elsie A. Holmes Nature Park, Georgia
trailData.description: The park is open daily from 9 am to 6 pm. The Elsie Holmes Nature Park offers a perfect recreational spot for visitors who want to enjoy nature. The park is bordered by South Chickamauga Creek and boasts five walking trails, excellent fishing spots, picnic areas, and peaceful, relaxing spots. The park also features a 1,500-square-foot screened-in pavilion for public use, and there are restrooms.

trailData.name: White Trail and Historic Trace Route
trailData.description: The Trace, or White Trail, is a point-to-point trail.  From its beginning at the Boling Park trailhead to its termination at the bridge at Jug Creek, the trail travels approximately four miles.  The first two miles, between Boling Park and the New Hightower church, are relatively flat and heavily travelled.  Clear-cut operations conducted on CCWSA property in the vicinity of the church have made the beginning of the second half of the trail harder to spot.  The first hundred yards past the...

trailData.name: Green Meadows Preserve Inner Loop
trailData.description: This route follows the interior trails in the park, forming a short loop with a great variety of terrain. The mowed grass and dirt trails wind through beautiful forest areas, open grass fields with limited shade, and benches for breaks. It is well-maintained and offers scenic variety, from green meadows to pine forests and gardens, with some sections close to the road. The trail can be muddy after rain. Wildlife is commonly seen, especially white-tail deer and many bird species.

trailData.name: Bunten Road Park Loop
trailData.description: The Bunten Road Park Loop is a 1.5 mile trail located in a 45 acre suburban sports park.  The loop consists of a ½ mile soft surfaced nature trail and a 1.0 mile asphalted multi-use circuit.  About half of the loop is wooded and the other half is open.  The wooded segment uses a series of switchbacks over steep grades and bridges over spring seeps.  The open segment circles around sport fields.  The ½ mile nature trail and 1.0 mile multi-use circuit are combined in this loop, but each can...

trailData.name: Christmas Trail
trailData.location_label: White Oak Mountain Trail System, Tennessee

trailData.name: Upper Truck to Bluff Trail Loop
trailData.description: This loop starts at a pull-off on the top of Lookout Mountain. Start by descending down the Bluff trail to John Smart trail and connect to the wide gravel path of Upper Truck. Take Gum Springs back up to the bluff and enjoy the beautiful views from the cliff band. The trail is shared with gravel/mountain bikers on Upper Truck and rock climbers on the Bluff trail.

trailData.name: Little Tallapoosa Park Trail
trailData.description: Little Tallapoosa Park Trail offers a nice mix of nature trails and paved trails bordering the Little Tallapoosa River. The park is pristine and has 256 acres of land. This multi-use trail is well marked and shared with hikers, bikers, and equestrians, so use proper trail etiquette. It can get muddy in some spots so come prepared.

trailData.name: Silver Comet Trail: Rockmart to Lower Coots Lake
Grassy Knob Vista Trail
trailData.description: The Grassy Knob Vista Trail is marked by blue blazes, and it takes you on a simple and peaceful path through the woods. Along the way, you will come across the Grassy Knob Rock Garden, which is an ideal spot to take a break and relax in the serene environment. If you want to extend your hike, you can consider adding on the Easle's Rest Trail, which features some beautiful viewing decks and other educational features that are worth exploring.

trailData.name: DeSoto Scout and Gilliam Loop
trailData.description:
This trail travels from DeSoto State Park(DSP) to the "Backcountry Trailhead" on Backcountry Road 5, in Little River Canyon National Preserve (LRCNP). The trail follows a backcountry road 5 to Edna Hill Church and is marked with "DST" signs, except within DSP where it is marked with a yellow blaze. 

Within DSP, the route runs along the bluff line from the northern border going south. It weaves around a few creeks and waterfalls that flow into the river. Past Indian Falls, the trail descends...

trailData.name: Deshier Monument

trailData.name: Van Michael Trail
trailData.description: This trail on the west side of the system offers plenty of ups and downs with mountain bike-optimized flow. Although mostly smooth, it is one of the most advanced trails at Blankets Creek due to its tight, twisting singletrack and the potential for high amplitude. Highlights include Kevorkian Pass, a steep, armored section with an incredible view of the lake, and The Gravity Cavity, a fast-rolling section that whips you around bermed turns like a roller coaster.

trailData.name: Dogwood, White Oak and Valley Trail
Dogwood, Hidden Spring, Rolling Green Loop
trailData.location_label: White Oak Mountain Trail System, Tennessee

trailData.name: Silver Comet Trail
trailData.description:
Venture through a tunnel & over three trestles on your magical rail-trail journey from Atlanta, GA to the Alabama border

This trail has it all. At over 60 miles in length, you'll have logged 120 miles round trip, so make plans to stay in either Rockmart or Cedartown because that's a lot of trail for one day.

You will enjoy crossing breathtaking trestles, tunneling under mountains, photographing unique birdhouses, visiting small-town Georgia, and meeting lots of smiling people along the way....

trailData.name: Lower Prince Loop
trailData.description: This route is a shared-use trail with easy terrain but includes some tight turns and light technical maneuvers that make for a great beginner-intermediate mountain biking trail. The Lower Prince Loop has the largest climb in the park at about 100 ft with an equally distant descent. The trail is well-maintained and has clear trail signage with many of the tight turns being bermed.

trailData.area_name: Garland Mountain Horse and Hiking Trails
trailData.name: Garland Mountain: West Side Loop
trailData.location_label: Garland Mountain Horse and Hiking Trails, Georgia
trailData.description:
Trails are periodically partially-closed here after periods of heavy rain or due to downed trees.

This loop is comprised of most of the west side trails of the Garland Mountain Horse and Hike Trails. This trail is only a fraction of the 19.7 miles of open trail to explore.

Trails included in this loop:
Sorrel
Greenway West
Chestnut
Roan
Greenway South
Crimson

trailData.name: Lower Canada Creek Falls Trail
trailData.description: Also known as Big Falls, this is one of the most photogenic waterfalls in the area! Located on Canada Creek, this path travels alongside the creek and showcases the natural beauty of the surrounding forestland. This section of trail could be a bit more rugged depending on the season, which is why it is not often traveled.

trailData.name: Clinton Walking Track and Yellow Trail Loop
trailData.description:
This park has a variety of short and gentle trails that are great for the whole family. This route includes two loops and passes by a small lake.

Accessibility: 

Equipment
Visitors using wheelchairs, mobility equipment, or strollers may need all-terrain tires or adaptive/motorized equipment for the surface type and grade.

Parking
There are several designated accessible spaces with striped access aisles in the paved parking lot off Ephesus Church Road. The trail can be accessed using a...

trailData.name: Laurel Creek Trail
trailData.description: The Laurel Creek Trail is one of several trails open to the public for hiking at the Davidson-Arabia Mountain Nature Preserve, located in Lithonia, Georgia. This easy to moderate trail offers an enjoyable 1.8 mile hike that combines scenic Georgia woodlands with the relaxing noise of the gently cascading waters of Laurel Creek.

trailData.name: East Roswell Park Loop
trailData.description:
This trail is just outside of Atlanta in Roswell and is a loop that goes along the perimeter of Roswell Park extending into the Seven Branches Property. The rugged terrain runs along a cascading creek with several small waterfalls. It is a beautiful mix of open areas and wooded areas. Dress accordingly! Seven Branches property includes a few creek crossings of shallow water. 

Users have reported the section of the trail on the north side of Eve's Road opposite the park is not well...

trailData.name: Hard Labor Creek State Park Red Loop
trailData.location_label: Hard Labor Creek State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: The Red Trail is the most challenging of the three major loops. Hand-built, old-school cross-country singletrack features roots, rocks, climbs, whoops and creek views. Not recommended for families or beginners. The trail is primarily used for mountain biking.

trailData.name: Hardy Trail
trailData.location_label: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Tennessee
trailData.description: There are parts of this route that is designated as foot trail only along the Mountain Beautiful Trail. For more information, please go here: https://www.nps.gov/chch/planyourvisit/upload/Lookout-Mountain-Battlefield-Trail-Map.pdf

trailData.name: Dog River Green Trail
trailData.description: This trail begins at the library trailhead and travels through the woods amongst a thick tree canopy to the Dog River and then loops back to the library. This is the longest trail in the system and offers a variety of sights and terrain.

trailData.name: Cherokee Bluffs Short Trail
trailData.description: This is the most direct and least strenuous path to the water features and the bluffs. There are many opportunities to view wildlife and local flowers along the way. The trail can become muddy during wet conditions and waterproof shoes are recommended.

trailData.name: Brown's Mill Outer Loop
trailData.description: This trail is intended to be multi-use and is shared by mountain bikers and hikers. The outer loop is the longest trail in the park and follows the perimeter of the park. Including this route, there are over 6 miles of trails to explore which can be combined to form longer alternate routes. The singletrack path is well-worn and easy to follow with clear blazes.

trailData.name: Lake Conasauga Picnic and Swim Site
Hard Labor Creek Orange, Purple and Blue Trail Loops
trailData.location_label: Hard Labor Creek State Park, Georgia
trailData.description: A very enjoyable set of trails. The Orange and Purple Loops are easy and are connectors to get to the Blue Loop. The Blue Loop has the more interesting shoals and water features. Mountain bikers are supposed to follow the direction for the appropriate day of the week.

trailData.name: Hembree Park Trail
trailData.description: The Hembree Park Trail is a great loop that has a soft surface and is located in a suburban sports park.  The highlights along the trail include a wooded area with specimen hardwood trees, a cascading creek, a memorial walk, and a contemplation pond.

trailData.name: Dragging Canoe - Little Owl Village - Chickamauga - Sarah Key Loop
trailData.description:
This is a non-profit nature sanctuary and the trails are maintained by volunteers. It is more of a walk in the woods than it is a strenuous hike. It's a great place to enjoy birds, insects, wildlife, history, archeology, and the South Chickamauga Creek. The property has both a put-in and take-out location for paddle sports in the summer. They also host lots of events throughout the year.

There is a day fee based on age. Children under 5 are...

options.systemMessage:
You are a helpful HR assistant designed to answer employee questions based on company policies.

Retrieve relevant information from the provided internal documents and provide a concise, accurate, and informative answer to the employee's question.

Use the tool called "company_documents_tool" to retrieve any information from the company's documents.

If the answer cannot be found in the provided documents, respond with "I cannot find the answer in the available resources."

parameters.name: company_documents_tool
parameters.description: Retrieve information from any company documents

parameters.content: ## Add docuemnts to vector store when updating or creating new documents in Google Drive

## Set up steps

1. Google Cloud Project and Vertex AI API:
* Create a Google Cloud project.
* Enable the Vertex AI API for your project.
2. Google AI API Key:
* Obtain a Google AI API key from Google AI Studio.
3. Pinecone Account:
* Create a free account on the Pinecone website.
Obtain your API key from your Pinecone dashboard.
* Create an index named company-files in your Pinecone project.
4. Google Drive:
* Create a dedicated folder in your Google Drive where company documents will be stored.
5. Credentials in n8n: Configure credentials in your n8n environment for:
* Google Drive OAuth2
* Google Gemini(PaLM) Api (using your Google AI API key)
* Pinecone API (using your Pinecone API key)
5. Import the Workflow:
* Import this workflow into your n8n instance.
6. Configure the Workflow:
* Update both Google Drive Trigger nodes to watch the specific folder you created in your Google Drive.
* Configure the Pinecone Vector Store nodes to use your company-files index.

values.content:
You are an AI Project Manager operating as the primary technical project management agent for this development project. Your core responsibilities are:

🎯 PROJECT MANAGEMENT ROLE:
- You ARE the Project Manager for this tech project - take ownership and lead
- Create comprehensive project boards with proper structure (Epics → Stories → Tasks)
- Establish realistic timelines and manage project milestones
- Coordinate between development teams and stakeholders
- Monitor project health, risks, and dependencies
- Provide regular status updates and recommendations

📋 BOARD STRUCTURE MANAGEMENT:
- Create EPICS board for high-level feature groupings
- Create TASKS board for detailed development work
- Create TIMELINES board for milestone and deadline tracking
- Create RETROS board for sprint retrospectives and improvements
- Ensure proper linking and dependencies between boards

🤝 PRODUCT MANAGER INTEGRATION:
- You receive requirements and direction from the Product Manager workflow
- Translate product requirements into technical implementation plans
- Break down product features into actionable development tasks
